records.title: chore(infra): cut outbound-HTTP jobs over to the worker gateway
records.issueTitle: chore(infra): cut outbound-HTTP jobs over to the worker gateway and delete in-process scraper paths
records.issueBody:
## Context

#962 and #963 add the `http-enrich` gateway capability/contracts and the `apps/worker` handlers for the 8 outbound-HTTP scraper jobs scoped by #960 (phase 2 tracker): NHTSA recalls/complaints/investigations/safety-ratings/manufacturer-communications, vin-enrich, model-research, fueleconomy-msrp, and dealer-enrich. Phase 1's cutover (#953) is the template: switch scheduling to dispatch via the gateway, then delete the now-dead in-process execution paths.

## Problem / Goal

Cut these 8 jobs over from in-process execution in `apps/scraper` to dispatch through the worker gateway (`apps/api` → `apps/worker`), then remove the superseded in-process job logic, following the phase-1 pattern in #953.

## Proposed approach

- Update job scheduling/registration (wherever `apps/scraper` currently enqueues/executes these 8 job types in-process) to dispatch through the worker gateway using the `http-enrich` capability contracts from #962.
- Delete the in-process job bodies in `apps/scraper/src/jobs/nhtsa-recalls.ts`, `nhtsa-complaints.ts`, `nhtsa-investigations.ts`, `nhtsa-safety-ratings.ts`, `nhtsa-manufacturer-communications.ts`, `vin-enrich.ts`, `model-research.ts`, `fueleconomy-msrp.ts`, `dealer-enrich.ts` (and now-unused shared helpers only used by them) once the gateway path is confirmed working, mirroring how #953 removed the direct-DB browser job paths.
- Verify job success rate and scheduling cadence for each migrated job against ops job-run dashboards before and after cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 8 jobs listed above are dispatched through the worker gateway and executed by `apps/worker`, not the in-process scraper daemon, verified by a passing dispatch/execution test or manual run recorded in the PR.
- [ ] The superseded in-process job bodies for these 8 jobs are deleted from `apps/scraper/src/jobs/`, with no remaining callers.
- [ ] Ops job-run dashboards show no regression in success rate or scheduling cadence for the migrated jobs after cutover (spot-checked and noted in the PR).

## Notes

Sequenced last in the #960 phase-2 breakdown, after #962 and #963. Related: #960 (parent tracker), #953 (phase-1 cutover this mirrors), #961 (phase 3: delete the scraper daemon entirely once nothing in-process remains).

records.title: feat(scraper): apps/worker handlers for outbound-HTTP enrichment jobs
records.issueTitle: feat(scraper): apps/worker handlers for outbound-HTTP enrichment jobs
records.issueBody:
## Context

#962 adds the `http-enrich` worker capability and gateway routing contracts for the outbound-HTTP scraper jobs identified in #960 (phase 2 tracker): NHTSA recalls/complaints/investigations/safety-ratings/manufacturer-communications, vin-enrich, model-research, fueleconomy-msrp, and dealer-enrich. Phase 1 (#952) already built the generic `apps/worker` runner and profile-gated job-runner compose service that executes dispatched jobs and submits results over authenticated HTTP without touching Postgres/Meilisearch/Valkey directly.

## Problem / Goal

Implement `apps/worker` handlers for the 8 outbound-HTTP jobs so they can execute on remote fleet workers under the `http-enrich` capability from #962, matching the existing job logic in `apps/scraper/src/jobs/` (HTTP calls, retry/jitter behavior, result shape) but without direct DB access — results are submitted back to the coordinator over HTTP per the phase-1 worker pattern.

## Proposed approach

- Add handler modules under `apps/worker/src/handlers/` for each of the 8 job types, porting the outbound-HTTP logic (using `fetchWithRetry`/jitter equivalents already used in `apps/scraper/src/jobs/nhtsa-*.ts`, `vin-enrich.ts`, `model-research.ts`, `fueleconomy-msrp.ts`, `dealer-enrich.ts`) to run against the zod contracts added in #962.
- Register the new handlers with the `http-enrich` capability declared by the worker on WS `hello` (per `WorkerCapabilities` from #962).
- Preserve job-specific behavior (NHTSA date parsing via `nhtsa-date-utils.ts`, dealer-enrich's Google Places auth) in the ported handlers.
- Add unit tests per handler mirroring the coverage in the corresponding `apps/scraper/src/jobs/*.test.ts` files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `apps/worker` has a handler for each of the 8 job types that produces output matching the corresponding `apps/scraper/src/jobs/*.ts` job's result contract, verified by unit tests.
- [ ] A worker instance advertising `http-enrich` capability can receive and execute a dispatched job of each type end-to-end against the gateway from #962 (integration or manual verification noted in the PR).
- [ ] No handler performs direct database, Meilisearch, or Valkey access — results are returned to the coordinator over HTTP only.

## Notes

Sequenced second in the #960 phase-2 breakdown, after #962 (contracts/capability). Related: #960 (parent tracker), #962, #952 (phase-1 worker runner this extends).

records.title: feat(queue): add http-enrich worker capability and gateway routing for outbound-HTTP jobs
records.issueTitle: feat(queue): add http-enrich worker capability and gateway routing for outbound-HTTP jobs
records.issueBody:
## Context

#960 (phase 2 tracker) scopes migrating the scraper's outbound-HTTP-only jobs (no Chromium/DOM dependency) onto the worker-gateway architecture built in phase 1 (#948-953). Confirmed candidate jobs, all reading `@wivwav/db` directly and calling `fetchWithRetry` against public/keyed HTTP APIs, no browser:

- `apps/scraper/src/jobs/nhtsa-recalls.ts`, `nhtsa-complaints.ts`, `nhtsa-safety-ratings.ts` → `api.nhtsa.gov`
- `apps/scraper/src/jobs/nhtsa-investigations.ts`, `nhtsa-manufacturer-communications.ts` → `www.nhtsa.gov`
- `apps/scraper/src/jobs/vin-enrich.ts` → `vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov`
- `apps/scraper/src/jobs/model-research.ts`, `fueleconomy-msrp.ts` → `www.fueleconomy.gov`
- `apps/scraper/src/jobs/dealer-enrich.ts` → `maps.googleapis.com` (Google Places, API-key auth)

Today `apps/api/src/worker-gateway/registry.ts` (`WorkerRegistry.pickWorker`) only distinguishes workers by a single `chromium: boolean` requirement (see `RegisteredWorker.capabilities: WorkerCapabilities` and `pickWorker(requirements: { chromium: boolean })`). None of these jobs need a browser, so they don't need chromium-capable workers, but the registry has no other capability dimension to route on yet.

## Problem / Goal

Extend the worker-protocol contracts and gateway routing so outbound-HTTP jobs can be dispatched to any non-Chromium worker under a shared `http-enrich` capability, without requiring per-source worker types. Per-source concurrency (avoiding parallel hits on the same upstream API) should reuse the existing `sourceLocks` mechanism in `WorkerRegistry` rather than introducing new locking.

## Proposed approach

- In `packages/types/src/worker-protocol.ts`, extend `WorkerCapabilities` with an `httpEnrich: boolean` flag (or equivalent capability set) alongside the existing `chromium` flag, and add zod payload/result contracts for the 8 job types listed above (mirroring the phase-1 `SOURCE_SCRAPE`/`DETAIL_CRAWL`/`DETAIL_EXTRACT` contract shapes).
- In `apps/api/src/worker-gateway/registry.ts`, extend `pickWorker` requirements to accept `{ chromium: boolean; httpEnrich: boolean }` (or a generalized capability list) so non-Chromium workers can be matched for these job types.
- In `apps/api/src/worker-gateway/dispatcher.ts`, route the 8 job types to workers advertising `httpEnrich`, reusing `tryAcquireSourceLock`/`releaseSourceLock` per upstream source id.
- Add/extend tests in `apps/api/src/worker-gateway/registry.test.ts` and `dispatcher.test.ts` for the new capability dimension.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `WorkerRegistry.pickWorker` can select a worker by `httpEnrich` capability independent of `chromium`, verified by a registry unit test with mixed-capability workers.
- [ ] Zod contracts exist in `packages/types` for all 8 outbound-HTTP job payload/result shapes and are exported for use by both `apps/api` and `apps/worker`.
- [ ] Dispatch routing for these job types acquires/releases the existing per-source lock exactly as SOURCE_SCRAPE does today, verified by a dispatcher test.

## Notes

Sequenced first in the #960 phase-2 breakdown (contracts/capability → worker handlers → cutover), mirroring the phase-1 sequence (#949 → #951/#952 → #953). No browser-relocation step is needed since none of these jobs touch Chromium. Related: #960 (parent tracker), #948-953 (phase-1 implementation).

records.title: chore(infra): cut browser jobs over to worker gateway
records.issueTitle: chore(infra): cut browser jobs over to the worker gateway and delete direct-DB scraper paths
records.issueBody:
## Context

Phase 1, step 5 (final) of the worker-fleet architecture (#948). All components exist; this issue flips production over and deletes the superseded direct-DB code paths from `apps/scraper`.

## Problem / Goal

Cut the three browser-job queues over from `apps/scraper`'s in-process workers to the coordinator gateway in one release, then remove the dead code.

## Proposed approach

- **Cutover (one release)**: remove the `SOURCE_SCRAPE`/`DETAIL_CRAWL`/`DETAIL_EXTRACT` worker registrations (and their now-unused imports: `PlaywrightBrowserService`, engine repositories, the two job runners) from `apps/scraper/src/index.ts`; enable `WORKER_GATEWAY_ENABLED` on the Mac Mini; start the `job-runner` container on the laptop with `COORDINATOR_URL` pointed at the Mac Mini's API. Schedule registration (`reconcileSchedules`) for these queues stays in `apps/scraper` — `queue.add` is processor-agnostic.
- **Cleanup (after stability window)**: delete `apps/scraper`'s three classes in `infrastructure/prisma-repositories.ts`, old `jobs/detail-crawl.ts`/`jobs/detail-extract.ts`, `application/listing-ingest.ts`, `resolution/card-claims.ts`/`claims-repository.ts` — grep first to confirm nothing else imports each before deleting; anything still imported stays and gets noted here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apps/scraper` registers no workers for the three browser queues (assert via runtime-mode/worker-registration test) while `reconcileSchedules` still registers their schedules unchanged.
- [ ] Post-cutover smoke: an operator-triggered source scrape (existing `/admin` enqueue route) completes end-to-end through the laptop worker, with the run visible in Bull Board and `ScraperRun` recorded.
- [ ] Chromium/Playwright is no longer a dependency of the `scraper` Docker image (image builds without it; image size drop recorded as evidence).
- [ ] Superseded files deleted with grep evidence per file that no remaining imports exist; monorepo typecheck/lint/build/tests green.
- [ ] Deployment section filled in: release notes, rollback plan (disable `WORKER_GATEWAY_ENABLED` + revert the worker-registration removal — the flag alone is not a rollback once registrations are deleted), and post-release smoke checks.

## Notes

Tracker: #948. Blocked by all four prior issues. Rollback nuance called out deliberately: after this lands, rolling back requires a revert deploy of `apps/scraper`, not just flipping the flag — the release notes must say so.

records.title: feat(scraper): generic apps/worker runner and profile-gated job-runner compose service
records.issueTitle: feat(scraper): generic apps/worker runner and profile-gated job-runner compose service
records.issueBody:
## Context

Phase 1, step 4 of the worker-fleet architecture (#948). With contracts, `packages/scraper-sources`, and the coordinator in place, build the generic worker runner and its container. The container is the laptop deployment vehicle and must never start on the Mac Mini's default stack.

## Problem / Goal

New app `apps/worker`: a generic job runner that dials an outbound WS to the coordinator, declares capabilities, executes dispatched jobs via a handler registry, and performs all persistence through `/internal/scraper/*` HTTP calls. Plus a `job-runner` docker-compose service gated behind `profiles: [worker]`.

## Proposed approach

- **`apps/worker`** (no `@wivwav/db` in `package.json` — the build-time invariant): WS client (dial `/internal/workers/ws`, send `WorkerHello`, reconnect with backoff, heartbeat), job-handler registry keyed by queue name, HTTP client for `/internal/scraper/*` (bearer auth, retry with backoff on network failure — safe because the endpoints are idempotent per #948).
- **Three handlers**: source-scrape runs `scraper-engine.ts` against new `HttpListingRepository`/`HttpSourceRepository`/`HttpScraperRunRepository` implementing the unchanged port interfaces from `apps/scraper/src/engine/repositories.ts`; detail-crawl and detail-extract are ported from `apps/scraper/src/jobs/` with every `db.*` call replaced by an HTTP call. Dealer enrichment (`blvd-dealer-enrichment.ts`) stays in the worker — plain fetch, it's scraping traffic.
- **Config** via env: `COORDINATOR_URL`, `WORKER_TOKEN`, `WORKER_CAPABILITIES` (e.g. `chromium=true`), `WORKER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS`.
- **`job-runner` compose service**: behind `profiles: [worker]` (same pattern as `ollama`'s `[ai]`); environment contains only the four vars above — no `DATABASE_URL`, no valkey URL, no Meilisearch key. Carry over the Chromium-in-Docker settings from the existing `scraper` service: `security_opt: seccomp=./docker/chromium-seccomp.json`, `ipc: host`, `init: true`, `tmpfs: /tmp:size=512m`. New `docker/worker/Dockerfile` (repo rule: include COPY/build steps for all `packages/*` it consumes).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apps/worker/package.json` has no `@wivwav/db` dependency and the app builds; the `job-runner` service env contains no `DATABASE_URL`/valkey/Meilisearch variables.
- [ ] `docker compose up` (default profiles) does not start `job-runner`; `docker compose --profile worker up` does, and it connects + heartbeats against a local api.
- [ ] End-to-end: a full source-scrape → detail-crawl → detail-extract cycle against a fixture source, run through worker + local coordinator, produces `Listing`/`ListingObservation`/`ListingFieldClaim`/`RawPage` rows matching a baseline captured from the current in-process scraper on the same fixture.
- [ ] Kill the worker mid-job and restart: the job is re-dispatched and completes with no duplicate rows (exercises reconnect + idempotent resubmission).
- [ ] A worker with `WORKER_CAPABILITIES` set to `chromium=false` never receives browser-queue jobs; they dispatch when a chromium-capable worker connects.

## Notes

Tracker: #948. Blocked by contracts, `packages/scraper-sources`, and the coordinator issues.

records.title: feat(api): worker gateway — WS dispatch, worker registry, and /internal/scraper ingest routes
records.issueTitle: feat(api): worker gateway — WS dispatch, worker registry, and /internal/scraper ingest routes
records.issueBody:
## Context

Phase 1, step 3 of the worker-fleet architecture (#948). `apps/api` becomes the job coordinator: it keeps owning BullMQ/valkey (internal detail behind `packages/queue` adapters) and gains a WS dispatch gateway plus HTTP ingest routes so remote workers never touch the DB/queue. Reverses #666 D2 (see #948).

## Problem / Goal

Three additions to `apps/api`, all gated behind a new `WORKER_GATEWAY_ENABLED` config flag (default off — the existing `apps/scraper` workers keep consuming the three queues until cutover):

1. **WS gateway** `apps/api/src/plugins/worker-gateway-ws.ts` (new dep `@fastify/websocket`): endpoint `/internal/workers/ws`, bearer-authenticated against `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` on the upgrade request's `Authorization` header (same fail-closed semantics as `apps/api/src/plugins/admin-auth.ts`). Maintains an in-memory worker registry: socket, declared capabilities from `WorkerHello`, in-flight count, last heartbeat.
2. **Dispatcher + gateway BullMQ workers** `apps/api/src/worker-gateway/`: registers as the BullMQ worker for `SOURCE_SCRAPE`/`DETAIL_CRAWL`/`DETAIL_EXTRACT` via the existing `packages/queue` worker adapter. Processor: pick an eligible worker (capability match, below its concurrency cap, per-source concurrency cap respected); if none connected, return a retry signal quickly — never block holding a job lock. On dispatch, await a promise in `Map<correlationId, {resolve, reject}>` resolved by the worker's final HTTP submission (same process), rejected on timeout/disconnect so BullMQ retries. Periodic `job.extendLock()` while genuinely in-flight; raised `lockDuration` for these queues.
3. **Ingest routes** `apps/api/src/routes/internal-scraper.ts` at `/internal/scraper`, using the `adminAuthPlugin`-wrapped-scope pattern (`apps/api/src/app.ts:298-345`). Backed by new classes in `apps/api/src/repositories/scraper-gateway/` (separate from the existing same-named admin repositories) that **port** `ingestListing` (`apps/scraper/src/application/listing-ingest.ts`), `recordCardFieldClaims`/`recordClaim`/`applyFieldResolution` (`apps/scraper/src/resolution/`), `recordDetailFieldClaims`, `markGone`, and detail-extract's Serializable transaction. Transactions keep their exact shape (`withTransientRetry(() => db.$transaction(..., Serializable))`), just invoked from route handlers. Request bodies validated with the shared zod contracts (`schema.parse()`).

Routes: run start/complete/fail; source transitions + mappings + drift-baseline; `POST /listings/upsert`; `POST /sources/:id/listings/mark-gone`; detail-crawl pending-listings + mark-gone; raw-page upsert + mark-processed; detail-extract pending-raw-pages + listing-by-source-url + `POST /detail-extract/submit`.

Idempotency requirements: `markGone`'s `missingFromCompleteCount` increment must be gated behind a per-`(sourceId, scraperRunId)` marker (mirrors the `enqueueRequiredListingResolution` marker pattern); `onGone` becomes a no-op (the `LISTING_INDEX_POLL` poller picks up status changes via `updatedAt`); `/listings/upsert` and `/detail-extract/submit` are already idempotent by construction — preserve that in the port.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `WORKER_GATEWAY_ENABLED` unset/false, `apps/api` registers no BullMQ workers and no WS route; existing behavior byte-identical (existing test suite unchanged and green).
- [ ] WS upgrade without/with wrong bearer token is rejected (401) and with the correct token accepted; fail-closed (503) in production when the secret is unset — matching `admin-auth.ts` semantics, with tests.
- [ ] With the flag on and no worker connected, an enqueued job stays in the queue (no starved lock) and is dispatched within one retry cycle of a capable worker connecting — integration test.
- [ ] `POST /internal/scraper/listings/upsert` and `POST /internal/scraper/detail-extract/submit` are idempotent: identical payload submitted twice → second response reports the no-op outcome and creates zero new listing/history/observation/claim rows — tests assert row counts.
- [ ] Repeated `mark-gone` for the same `(sourceId, scraperRunId)` does not double-increment `missingFromCompleteCount` — test.
- [ ] Ported ingest produces identical DB rows to `apps/scraper`'s in-process path for the same fixture input (regression fixture comparison against `listing-ingest.ts` behavior).

## Notes

Tracker: #948. Blocked by the contracts issue. The dispatcher's per-source concurrency cap can start as a simple "one in-flight job per sourceId" rule — fleet-scale fairness is out of scope for phase 1.

records.title: chore(scraper): relocate browser layer and Chromium source adapters into packages/scraper-sources
records.issueTitle: chore(scraper): relocate browser layer and Chromium source adapters into packages/scraper-sources
records.issueBody:
## Context

Phase 1, step 2 of the worker-fleet architecture (#948). The future `apps/worker` must have no `@wivwav/db` dependency (build-time enforcement of "workers never touch the DB"), but the browser layer and source adapters it needs currently live inside `apps/scraper`, which depends on `@wivwav/db`.

## Problem / Goal

Relocate (not duplicate) the browser layer and the three Chromium source adapters plus their parsing dependents out of `apps/scraper` into a new shared package `packages/scraper-sources`, so both `apps/scraper` (until cutover) and the future `apps/worker` can import them. Behavioral no-op.

## Proposed approach

- Move `apps/scraper/src/browser/` and, from `apps/scraper/src/sources/`: `blvd.ts`, `freedom-motors.ts`, `mobilityworks.ts`, `blvd-detail.ts`, `mobilityworks-detail.ts`, `declarative-detail.ts`, `source-listing-dates.ts`, `blvd-dealer-enrichment.ts`, `field-transforms.ts`, `image-filter.ts` (+ their co-located tests) into `packages/scraper-sources`.
- Seed jobs also living in `sources/` (`conversion-brands.ts`, `nmeda-dealers.ts`) and `registry.ts`'s DB-touching source upsert stay in `apps/scraper`. Verify the exact boundary against `registry.ts` imports before moving — anything the moved files import that touches `@wivwav/db` indicates a boundary error, not something to drag along.
- Update `apps/scraper` imports; update all three Dockerfiles (api, scraper, migrate — repo rule: a new `packages/*` requires COPY + build steps in every Dockerfile).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/scraper-sources/package.json` has no dependency on `@wivwav/db` (and no transitive import of it — verified by build).
- [ ] `apps/scraper` builds and its full existing test suite passes with only import-path changes (no logic edits in moved files).
- [ ] All three Docker images build successfully with the new package's COPY/build steps.
- [ ] `conversion-brands.ts`, `nmeda-dealers.ts`, and the DB-touching parts of `registry.ts` remain in `apps/scraper`.

## Notes

Tracker: #948. Independent of the contracts issue — can land in parallel. Mechanical move; keep the diff reviewable by avoiding any refactoring beyond import paths.

records.title: feat(queue): add worker-protocol and scraper-gateway zod contracts to packages/types
records.issueTitle: feat(queue): add worker-protocol and scraper-gateway zod contracts to packages/types
records.issueBody:
## Context

Phase 1, step 1 of the worker-fleet architecture (#948). Workers and the coordinator need runtime-validated shared request/response shapes; `packages/types` today holds compile-time-only TS interfaces (no zod), and the API's TypeBox schemas live route-side in `apps/api` and aren't shared.

## Problem / Goal

Add zod contracts to `packages/types` for (a) the worker WS protocol envelope and (b) the three phase-1 job types' HTTP request/response bodies. Both `apps/api` (route handlers call `schema.parse()`; TypeBox stays reserved for the public `/v1/*` surface) and the future `apps/worker` HTTP client import these as the single source of truth.

## Proposed approach

New files `packages/types/src/worker-protocol.ts` and `packages/types/src/scraper-gateway.ts` (zod is already a dependency of both consumer apps; add it to `packages/types` if absent):

- **Protocol envelope**: `WorkerHello` (capabilities: `chromium: boolean`, `maxConcurrentJobs`, worker name/id), `WsJobDispatchMessage` (correlation id `${queueName}:${jobId}`, queue name, payload), `WsJobAckMessage`, `WsHeartbeatMessage`.
- **Job contracts**, mirroring the port interfaces in `apps/scraper/src/engine/repositories.ts`: `ScraperRunStart/Complete/Fail`; all `Source*` transitions + mappings + drift-baseline get/set; `ListingUpsertRequest/Response` (mirrors `ListingUpsertData`/`ListingUpsertResult`); `MarkGone` (with `scraperRunId` for the idempotency marker, see #948 notes); plus shapes with no port today: detail-crawl pending-listings read, raw-page upsert + mark-processed, detail-extract pending-raw-pages read, listing-by-source-url lookup, `DetailExtractSubmitRequest/Response`.

Export inferred TS types alongside each schema. No behavior change anywhere — pure addition.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/types` exports zod schemas + inferred types for the WS envelope (`WorkerHello`, `WsJobDispatchMessage`, `WsJobAckMessage`, `WsHeartbeatMessage`) and every phase-1 job contract listed above.
- [ ] `ListingUpsertRequest`/`Response` round-trips every field of `ListingUpsertData`/`ListingUpsertResult` from `apps/scraper/src/engine/repositories.ts` (compile-time assignability test in both directions).
- [ ] Unit tests: valid fixtures parse; fixtures with missing/mistyped required fields are rejected with field-level errors.
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, and full tests pass across the monorepo with no changes required in consuming apps.

## Notes

Tracker: #948. Blocks the coordinator (#948 step 3) and worker (#948 step 4) issues. Date-bearing fields cross the wire as ISO strings — schemas use `z.coerce.date()` (or explicit ISO-string types) so both sides agree; do not assume `Date` objects survive JSON.

records.title: feat(api): add get_diagnostic_context, get_system_snapshot, get_correlation diagnostic endpoints
records.issueTitle: feat(api): add get_diagnostic_context, get_system_snapshot, get_correlation diagnostic endpoints
records.issueBody:
## Context

#757 ratified the minimum read-only diagnostic contract. This issue builds the three new endpoints on top of the diagnostic auth scope (#773) and the shared domain snapshot (#774). The remaining tools in the MVP (`get_source_pipeline`, `get_recent_logs`, `get_failed_job`) are bounded/typed wrappers over existing `/admin` routes and are exposed later through the MCP adapter (follow-up issue), not new API routes.

## Problem / Goal

Add three new routes under `/diagnostics/*`:

- **`get_diagnostic_context`**: mostly-static versioned content — service/queue semantics, signal glossary, runbook index, safety rules, required facts/hypotheses/unknowns/next-checks response protocol — plus live deployed build/revision metadata (fixed response size).
- **`get_system_snapshot`**: the #774 domain snapshot, windowed (≤24h, default 1h), with per-section item caps and `signalAvailability` reporting which backends were reachable.
- **`get_correlation(idType, id, window)`**: joins logs/jobs/runs/source state by an allow-listed `idType` (MVP: `jobId`, `sourceId`, `requestId`), capped at 100 log lines with truncation markers.

All responses must exclude decrypted configuration, credentials, cookies, and tokens, and must not accept arbitrary SQL/LogQL/URLs/filesystem paths — only allow-listed typed filters with bounded time windows and result counts.

## Proposed approach

- New route file(s) under `apps/api/src/routes/diagnostics/*`, registered behind the `#773` diagnostic-auth plugin.
- `get_diagnostic_context`: generate the static portion from repo content (service/queue semantics, runbook index) at build or route-init time; merge with live revision metadata.
- `get_system_snapshot`: call the #774 domain module; apply window/cap bounds.
- `get_correlation`: implement the allow-listed join across existing per-source pipeline, BullMQ job, run, and Loki log queries, reusing existing bounded-Loki-timeout patterns from `admin-logs.ts`.
- Update `docs/api-routes.md` with the three new routes, their bounds, and example typed request/response payloads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `get_diagnostic_context` returns fixed-size content including deployed revision metadata, and does not vary with system state.
- [ ] `get_system_snapshot` respects the ≤24h/default-1h window and per-section caps, and reports `signalAvailability` when a backend (e.g. Loki) is deliberately made unreachable in a test.
- [ ] `get_correlation` rejects `idType` values outside the allow-list (`jobId`, `sourceId`, `requestId`) and caps returned log lines at 100 with a truncation marker when exceeded.
- [ ] No response from any of the three routes includes decrypted config, credentials, cookies, or tokens (verified by a fixture test with a planted secret-shaped value).
- [ ] `docs/api-routes.md` is updated with the three routes and example payloads.

## Notes

Depends on #773 (diagnostic auth scope) and #774 (shared domain snapshot). Ratified in #757 (Q1, Q2, Q7 MVP list). `diagnose` is intentionally NOT a gateway endpoint (D1, accepted by Codex) — these three routes are evidential only. Response sanitization beyond secret-shaped fixtures is handled by the dedicated sanitizer issue.

records.title: feat(ops,scraper): surface job-run tree on source detail page and populate run stats
records.issueTitle: feat(ops,scraper): surface job-run tree on source detail page and populate run stats
records.issueBody:
## Context

`#933` shipped a `JobRun` model, per-job-type run tracking, and `GET /admin/sources/:id/job-runs` (a full pipeline run tree for a source, verified working against `main` via `make up`: real parent/child nesting across `source-scrape`, `detail-crawl`, `detail-extract`, `listing-resolve`). Nothing in `apps/ops` calls this endpoint yet — the data exists but no operator can see it.

Separately, `succeededCount`/`failedCount` on `JobRun` are `null` for effectively every run today. `withJobRunTracking` (`apps/scraper/src/lib/job-run-tracking.ts`) accepts optional `stats`, but most job processors never pass them, so a runs list would show status/timing with no indication of how much work succeeded or failed within a run.

## Problem / Goal

Add a "Runs" section to the existing source detail view that renders the job-run tree from `GET /admin/sources/:id/job-runs`, and wire up `succeededCount`/`failedCount` for the job types that don't populate them today, so the panel is actually useful rather than timing-only.

## Proposed approach

- `apps/ops/src/app/ops/sources/` (`SourcesClient.tsx` / source detail route): add a "Runs" section rendering the tree from `GET /admin/sources/:id/job-runs` — job type, status, started/finished timestamps, succeeded/failed counts, nested by `parentRunId` (indent or a simple nested list, no drag/panel work — this is a plain page section, not a `Workspace` panel).
- Failed runs show `errorMessage` inline.
- `apps/scraper`: for each job processor currently omitting `stats` in its `withJobRunTracking` call, pass `succeededCount`/`failedCount` where the processor already knows these numbers (e.g. detail-extract's per-page success/fail count, dedupe's merge count, vin-enrich's per-listing outcome count). Audit all callers of `withJobRunTracking` in `apps/scraper/src/index.ts` and fill in stats wherever the processor has the numbers on hand already; for job types with no natural success/fail count (if any), leave `stats` omitted rather than fabricating one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The source detail page renders a Runs section sourced from `GET /admin/sources/:id/job-runs`, showing job type, status, timestamps, and nested children by `parentRunId`, verified by a component test with a fixture tree (multi-level, at least one failed run).
- [ ] A failed run's `errorMessage` is visible in the Runs section, verified by the same or an additional component test.
- [ ] At least `detail-extract`, `deduplicate`, and `vin-enrich` job runs report non-null `succeededCount`/`failedCount` after a real run, verified by extending or adding to `apps/scraper/src/lib/job-run-tracking.integration.test.ts` for each of those job types.
- [ ] Manual QA: with `make dev` (or `make up`) running, open a source's detail page, confirm the Runs section shows recent activity across multiple job types with correct nesting, and confirm at least one run type from the acceptance criteria above shows non-null counts.

## Notes

- Explicitly not the `docked-terminal`/`Workspace` panel treatment — that's tracked separately in `#934` and depends on the `#912`/`#913` Overview decision. This issue is a plain page section on the existing source detail route, independent of that decision.
- Does not address `Listing.lastRunId` only being set by the scrape pipeline (geocode/dedupe/vin-enrich don't set it on their writes yet) — noted as a known gap in `#933`'s PR, left as a future follow-up, not in scope here.
- Does not touch `#775` (diagnostic `get_correlation` endpoint, still open) — that issue should separately be updated to consume `JobRun` instead of the ad hoc per-source pipeline join it currently proposes, but that's its own change.

records.title: feat(db,api): job/run lineage backbone — trace a source through every job type
records.issueTitle: feat(db,api): job/run lineage backbone — trace a source through every job type down to results
records.issueBody:
## Context

Today, traceability from a `Source` (e.g. blvd.com) to what happened to it is fragmented and mostly missing:

- Only the initial scrape stage persists a run record (`ScraperRun` in `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`, keyed by `sourceId`), and that column has no declared Prisma `@relation` to `Source` (plain unconstrained column).
- All later pipeline stages — detail-crawl, detail-extract, geocode, dedupe, vin-enrich, nhtsa-recalls/complaints/safety-ratings, listing-sync (see `getCanonicalDefs()` in `apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts`) — persist no run record at all. Status only exists transiently in BullMQ; once a job finishes, there is no DB record it ever ran.
- Most of those later job types aren't source-scoped (`data: {}` in their job definitions, `admin.ts` ~L701-708) — no way to filter "what happened to blvd.com's data" past the scrape stage.
- `Listing.sourceId` links each vehicle back to its source, but not to the specific `ScraperRun` (or any run) that produced it.
- No DB log table exists; logs live only in stdout/pino and Sentry, uncorrelated to source or run in any queryable way.

This gap blocks the operator workflow: click a red source, see its full pipeline run tree end-to-end, drill into the failing step, see its logs and the vehicles it touched. It's also the missing backbone under `#757`'s `get_correlation` diagnostic endpoint and the `docked-terminal` workspace (`#913`), both of which currently can only correlate what already has an ID to correlate with.

## Problem / Goal

Build the data model and API layer so a source's full pipeline (scrape → crawl → extract → geocode → dedupe → vin-enrich → listing-sync, etc.) can be traced end to end: source → all its runs across every job type → per-run stats/errors → the individual listings that run produced.

## Proposed approach

- Add a generic `JobRun` model to `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`, used by every job type (not just scrape): `id`, `jobType`, `sourceId` (nullable, with a declared `@relation` to `Source`), `parentRunId` (self-relation, so a scrape run's spawned crawl/extract runs form a tree), `status`, `startedAt`, `finishedAt`, stat counters (succeeded/failed/etc.), `errorMessage`.
- Thread `sourceId` through the currently-global job payloads (geocode, dedupe, vin-enrich, nhtsa-*, listing-sync) wherever the work is attributable to a source, so those runs become filterable by source too.
- Add `Listing.lastRunId` (FK to `JobRun`) so a vehicle can be traced back to the run that last produced/touched it.
- Tag structured log fields (pino) with `runId` so logs stay correlatable per run without introducing a new DB log table (decide finer details of log correlation during implementation).
- Add API endpoint(s) (e.g. under `/admin` or a new `/diagnostics` route consistent with `#757`'s contract) to fetch a source's run tree and a run's stats/logs/results — sufficient to back a drill-down UI panel later.
- Migrate/backfill: keep `ScraperRun` or fold it into `JobRun` (implementer's call) — either way, existing scrape-run history should not be silently lost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `JobRun` rows are created for every job type in `getCanonicalDefs()` (not just scrape), each with a correct `jobType`, `status`, and `sourceId` where applicable, verified by a test per job type.
- [ ] A `JobRun` spawned by another (e.g. an extract run triggered by a scrape run) has a `parentRunId` pointing to its parent, verified by a test asserting the resulting tree shape for at least one multi-stage pipeline.
- [ ] Given a `Listing`, its `lastRunId` resolves to the `JobRun` that last touched it, verified by a test.
- [ ] An API endpoint returns a source's full run tree (all job types, correctly nested by `parentRunId`) filtered to that source, verified by an integration test.
- [ ] `docs/api-routes.md` is updated with the new endpoint(s).

## Notes

- Companion issue (`docked-terminal` workspace live-update/lineage-panel delta) tracked separately — this issue is the data/API backbone only, no UI work.
- Coordinate with `#757`/`#775`'s `get_correlation` diagnostic endpoint so both consume the same `JobRun` model rather than forking correlation logic.
- No dependency on the closed D7 architecture gate (`#666`) — `#675`'s exit criterion is already satisfied.

records.title: feat(api): add asymmetric diagnostic auth scope (DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET)
records.issueTitle: feat(api): add asymmetric diagnostic auth scope (DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET)
records.issueBody:
## Context

#757 ratified a read-only AI diagnostic gateway. Both Claude's review (D2) and Codex's ratification require a **separate** credential from `INTERNAL_API_SECRET`, because the desktop-client requirement (Claude/ChatGPT desktop apps) means a bearer token will sit in a plaintext desktop MCP config file. `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` currently unlocks queue mutation, schedule changes, and `GET /admin/config/:key/decrypt` — handing that to a desktop AI client is unacceptable.

Relevant files: `apps/api/src/plugins/admin-auth.ts` (the fail-closed pattern to mirror), `docs/api-routes.md`.

## Problem / Goal

Add a new fail-closed auth plugin/scope for a `/diagnostics/*` route prefix, gated by `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET`, with the same 503-in-production-when-unset semantics as `admin-auth.ts`.

Credential relationship must be asymmetric:
- `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET` is accepted only on `/diagnostics/*`.
- `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` may also be accepted on `/diagnostics/*` (so the ops BFF can proxy without new wiring) — this is an intentional, documented compatibility choice.
- `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET` must never be accepted on `/admin/*`.
- Enforcement is route-scoped via a plugin hook (like `admin-auth.ts`), not per-handler checks.

No diagnostic routes exist yet in this issue's scope — this issue only lands the auth plugin and scope, verified with a placeholder or the first real route from a follow-up issue.

## Proposed approach

- Add `apps/api/src/plugins/diagnostic-auth.ts` mirroring the structure of `admin-auth.ts`.
- Register it on a `/diagnostics` route prefix.
- Read `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET` from env; fail closed (503) in production when unset, matching existing admin-auth behavior.
- Document the asymmetric credential relationship in `docs/api-routes.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A request to any `/diagnostics/*` route with a valid `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET` bearer token succeeds; with no token or an invalid token it is rejected (401/403).
- [ ] A request to `/diagnostics/*` with a valid `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` succeeds (asymmetric compatibility).
- [ ] A request to any `/admin/*` route using `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET` is rejected — this credential never unlocks admin routes.
- [ ] In production with `DIAGNOSTIC_API_SECRET` unset, `/diagnostics/*` fails closed (503), matching `admin-auth.ts` semantics.
- [ ] `docs/api-routes.md` documents the new scope and the asymmetric credential relationship.

## Notes

Ratified in #757 (disagreement D2, Codex's "Credential and audit clarification" section). Part of the new "AI Diagnostic Gateway" milestone. This issue only adds the auth boundary; actual diagnostic endpoints are a follow-up issue.

records.title: feat(ops): surface missing-coordinate count on ops overview
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): surface missing-coordinate count on ops overview
records.issueBody:
## Context
The ops overview page has a hardcoded telemetry tile for `missing-coordinates` (`apps/ops/src/app/ops/overview-helpers.ts:214-221`) whose value is fixed to `'Not yet tracked'`, with detail text: "The API does not currently expose a missing-coordinate count. Use the geocode queue status as the available proxy."

The underlying data already exists: `ListingRepository.countActiveMissingCoordinates()` (`apps/api/src/repositories/listing-repository.ts:660`) is already computed and returned as `listings.missingLocations` in the `GET /admin/listing-refresh/status` response (`apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts:520-599`). No new DB query or API route is needed — the ops frontend simply never wired it in.

## Problem / Goal
Wire the existing `missingLocations` count into the ops overview `missing-coordinates` telemetry tile instead of showing the hardcoded "Not yet tracked" placeholder.

- `apps/ops/src/app/ops/use-overview-resources.ts`: add/extend a polled resource that fetches `/admin/listing-refresh/status` (or reuses an existing fetch of it) and exposes `listings.missingLocations`.
- `apps/ops/src/app/ops/overview-helpers.ts:214-221`: replace the hardcoded `value: 'Not yet tracked'` for the `missing-coordinates` card with the live count, using the existing `geocode-readiness` tile (lines 193-199) as the pattern for how a queue-derived stat is rendered.
- `apps/ops/src/app/ops/OpsOverviewClient.tsx:76,94`: confirm the existing `MapPin` icon/severity mapping for `missing-coordinates` still applies to the live value (e.g. severity thresholds for a nonzero count).

## Proposed approach
1. In `use-overview-resources.ts`, fetch `/admin/listing-refresh/status` (or extend the existing consumer of that endpoint) and surface `listings.missingLocations` alongside the data already used for `geocode-readiness`.
2. In `overview-helpers.ts`, update the `missing-coordinates` card builder to consume that count, formatting it consistently with other numeric telemetry tiles, and set severity (e.g. warning) when the count is above zero.
3. Update the tile's detail text so it no longer claims the count is unavailable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The ops overview `missing-coordinates` tile displays the live count from `listings.missingLocations` instead of the hardcoded `'Not yet tracked'` string.
- [ ] The tile's severity/icon reflects a nonzero missing-coordinate count (e.g. warning state) and a healthy state when the count is zero, consistent with the `geocode-readiness` tile's pattern.
- [ ] Manual QA: load `/ops` overview in a local environment with at least one listing missing lat/lng and confirm the tile shows the correct count and updates on refresh.

## Notes
Backend support already exists and requires no changes — see `countActiveMissingCoordinates()` in `apps/api/src/repositories/listing-repository.ts:660` and its use in `apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts:526-528,586-587`.

records.title: feat(api): expose last successful Meilisearch sync time via admin API
records.issueTitle: feat(api): expose last successful Meilisearch sync time via admin API
records.issueBody:
## Context
`POST /admin/sync` (apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts:390-397) enqueues a manual full re-index of the Meilisearch listings index, but there is no way to see when the last sync actually completed. The only existing signal is the Prometheus gauge `wivwav_meilisearch_last_sync_timestamp_seconds` (apps/api/src/routes/metrics.ts:27-34, 161-165), which is scrape-only and not consumable by an admin UI or operator tooling that wants a simple "synced N minutes ago" readout.

## Problem / Goal
Expose the last successful `listing-sync` completion time through the admin API so it doesn't require scraping `/metrics`.

Add a `GET /admin/sync` route in apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts, alongside the existing `POST /admin/sync`, that returns the last completed job's timestamp for the `listing-sync` queue.

## Proposed approach
- Extract `latestCompletedTimestampSeconds()` (currently private to apps/api/src/routes/metrics.ts:27-34) into a shared helper both metrics.ts and admin.ts can call, rather than duplicating the BullMQ `getJobs(['completed'])` lookup.
- Add `app.get('/sync', ...)` in admin.ts that calls the shared helper against `QUEUES.LISTING_SYNC` and returns `{ data: { lastSyncCompletedAt: string | null } }` (ISO 8601, or `null` when no completed job exists yet).
- No new persistence needed — BullMQ job history is the existing source of truth, consistent with the metrics endpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `GET /admin/sync` returns `lastSyncCompletedAt` as an ISO timestamp reflecting the most recently completed `listing-sync` job, or `null` when none has completed
- [ ] The Prometheus metric and the new endpoint share one implementation of the "latest completed job timestamp" lookup (no duplicated query logic)
- [ ] Automated test covers both the populated and empty (`null`) cases for `GET /admin/sync`

## Notes
Scraper's single-owner indexer job (#669 area) performs the actual rebuild; this endpoint only reports on job completion state already tracked in BullMQ, matching the pattern used by `POST /admin/sync`.

records.title: feat(web): visual hierarchy pass on vehicle detail page
records.issueTitle: feat(web): visual hierarchy pass on vehicle detail page — sparklines and status badges over raw tables/lists
records.issueBody:
## Context

The vehicle detail page (`apps/web/src/app/[locale]/listings/[id]/`) has substantial data already fetched and rendered per tab (price history, safety ratings/recalls, market pricing percentiles, model research claims), but it's presented largely as structured text/lists — everything reads at similar visual weight, so nothing stands out as more or less important. #919–#921 add more data to the same tabs; this issue is about presentation of what's already there (and whatever those land), not new data sources.

## Problem / Goal

Give the highest-signal facts (safety rating, recall status, price-vs-market position, listing freshness) a distinct visual treatment — badges, sparklines, a small stat strip — so a buyer can scan the page and immediately see what matters, with denser detail available but not shouting at the same volume as the headline facts.

## Proposed approach

- `OverviewTab.tsx` price history: replace or supplement the current price-history table/list with a compact sparkline (small inline chart, not a full-size chart component) showing trend direction at a glance.
- `SafetyTab.tsx`: recall status (`openRecallCount`, already computed in `detail-page.tsx:277`) and overall NHTSA rating as a single colored badge/stat near the top of the tab, ahead of the full recall/complaint lists.
- `MarketTab.tsx`: represent this listing's price against the `marketPricing.priceCents` percentile band (p10–p90) as a small horizontal position indicator rather than only listing the percentile numbers.
- Keep changes additive/visual — no data fetching changes, no new API calls. Follow `docs/BRAND.md` (required reading for `apps/web` UI edits per project convention) for color/type choices, particularly for any new semantic-status colors (recall open vs. remedied, price above/below market).
- Scope explicitly excludes the ops app and anything under `apps/ops` — that's a separate, unrelated command-center effort already tracked (#911–#915).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Safety tab shows a single at-a-glance status indicator (badge or equivalent) for recall/rating status above the detailed recall/complaint lists, without removing the detailed lists.
- [ ] Market tab visually represents this listing's price position relative to the market percentile band, in addition to the existing numeric percentiles.
- [ ] No new network requests are introduced — component tests confirm existing tab components render with the same props/data they already receive.
- [ ] Manual QA: review all five tabs (WAV, Vehicle, Overview, Market, Safety) on a real listing in both light and dark theme, confirming the new visual elements don't crowd out or visually compete with each other.

## Notes
This is the "make it feel considered, not just data-dumped" polish pass referenced in earlier design discussion — deliberately scoped after #919–#921 land, since those add sections that should also get this treatment rather than needing a second pass.

records.title: feat(web): VIN re-listing history timeline
records.issueTitle: feat(web): VIN re-listing price/mileage history timeline on vehicle detail page
records.issueBody:
## Context

#454 built `GET /v1/vin/:vin/history` (`apps/api/src/routes/vin.ts:98`), which calls `ListingRepository.findHistoryByVin` — a merged, chronologically-sorted price + mileage timeline spanning *every* listing that has ever existed for that VIN (re-listings across dealers and time), not just the current listing's own price history. This is separate from and richer than the already-shipped current-listing price chart (#516, `OverviewTab.tsx`), which only covers `ListingPriceHistory` for the single listing being viewed.

The catch: `/v1/vin/:vin/history` is PRO-tier gated (`tierAtLeast` check in `vin.ts`, returns `upgrade_required` for FREE tier). The web app's server-side `apiFetch` (`apps/web/src/lib/api-fetch.ts`) authenticates via `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` bearer bypass, not a registered API key — `resolveApiKeyTier` (`apps/api/src/services/api-key-tier.ts`) only recognizes tiers via `ApiKeyRepository.findActiveByHash`, so a bearer token that isn't a real hashed key resolves to `FREE` and would currently get rejected by this route. This needs to be resolved as part of the implementation, not assumed away.

## Problem / Goal

Show a "history across listings" chart on the vehicle detail page (only when a VIN exists and history spans more than the current listing) — price and mileage trend over the vehicle's full observed lifetime, distinct from the current single-listing price history already shown.

## Proposed approach

- Resolve the tier-gating gap first: either (a) have the internal bypass in `plugins/api-key-auth.ts` also short-circuit `resolveApiKeyTier` to the highest tier when `INTERNAL_API_SECRET` auth was used, or (b) mint/reuse an internal ENTERPRISE-tier `ApiKey` row for the web app's server-to-server calls. Confirm which pattern existing internal-to-internal calls (e.g. `/admin/config/:key/decrypt`) already use and follow it rather than introducing a third auth pattern.
- Add `getVinHistory(vin)` fetcher in `detail-page.tsx` (skip when `listing.vin` is null — many listings won't have one).
- New chart component distinguishing "this listing" from "other listings for this VIN" (e.g. a vertical marker or color break at each listing-source change), reusing whatever charting approach #516's price-history chart already established for visual consistency.
- Only render the section when the VIN history actually spans more than one listing — a single-listing VIN duplicates the existing price-history chart and shouldn't show twice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A VIN with re-listing history across 2+ listings renders a combined price + mileage timeline distinct from the single-listing price chart.
- [ ] A listing whose VIN has only ever appeared as this one listing does not render a duplicate/redundant history section.
- [ ] The web app's server-side call to `/v1/vin/:vin/history` succeeds (not `upgrade_required`) using whatever internal-auth resolution this issue implements — covered by an API test asserting the internal bypass resolves to a tier that passes `tierAtLeast(..., 'PRO')`.
- [ ] Manual QA: load a real multi-listing VIN in dev and confirm the timeline renders correctly on both light and dark theme.

## Notes
`findHistoryByVin`'s `findMany` calls are intentionally unbounded (see comment at `listing-repository.ts:560` from #454) — fine at current VIN re-listing depths, flagged there for revisit only if this becomes a hot path.

records.title: feat(web): surface WAV conversion-status history on vehicle detail page
records.issueTitle: feat(web): surface WAV conversion-status history on vehicle detail page
records.issueBody:
## Context

`ListingConversionHistory` (`listing_conversion_history` table) is actively written by the scraper on every ingest pass (`apps/scraper/src/application/listing-ingest.ts`), recording `conversionStatus` and `wavFeatures` snapshots over time per listing. Unlike `ListingPriceHistory`/`ListingMileageHistory`, it has **zero readers anywhere** — no repository method, no API route, no frontend usage. The data has been collected since #223 but was never wired to any consumer.

## Problem / Goal

Surface conversion-status changes (e.g. "converted" → "verified", or a WAV feature added/removed between scrapes) on the WAV tab of the vehicle detail page, giving buyers visibility into whether the conversion details have been amended or newly confirmed since the listing first appeared — a meaningful trust signal for a WAV-specific marketplace.

## Proposed approach

- Add a `findConversionHistory(listingId)` method to `ListingRepository` (mirrors the existing `listingPriceHistory`/`listingMileageHistory` query patterns already in the same file).
- Add `GET /v1/listings/:id/conversion-history` route (mirrors `/:id/price-history`).
- Add `getConversionHistory(id)` fetcher in `detail-page.tsx`, threaded into `WavTab.tsx`.
- Render only when there's more than one distinct entry — most listings will have a single unchanging snapshot and shouldn't show a "history" UI for that case.
- Keep the display simple (a short changelog list: date + what changed), not a chart — `conversionStatus` and `wavFeatures` are categorical, not continuous series.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A listing with 2+ distinct `ListingConversionHistory` rows shows a changelog of conversion-status/WAV-feature changes on the WAV tab.
- [ ] A listing with only one snapshot (the common case) does not render an empty or single-entry "history" section.
- [ ] New `findConversionHistory` repository method has a test asserting correct ordering (chronological) and listing-scoping.
- [ ] Manual QA: confirm rendering on a listing seeded with multiple conversion-history rows in dev, both light and dark theme.

## Notes
Lower priority than the dealer-ratings (#919) and VIN-history (#920) issues — this is a smaller, more niche signal. Good candidate to batch with #920 if a worker picks up both, since both add a small new history route following the same `/:id/price-history` pattern.

records.title: feat(web): surface dealer ratings, review count, hours, and reviews on the vehicle detail page
records.issueTitle: feat(web): surface dealer ratings, review count, hours, and reviews on the vehicle detail page
records.issueBody:
## Context

#103 built Google Places dealer enrichment (`apps/scraper/src/jobs/dealer-enrich.ts`) — it's live, populating `DealerProfile.rating`/`reviewCount`/`hours`/`googlePlaceId` and up to 5 `DealerReview` rows per dealer (author, rating, text, source, publishedAt), gated behind `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`. The API already exposes this data: `GET /v1/listings/:id/dealer` returns the `DealerProfile` (rating/reviewCount/hours), and `GET /v1/dealers/:id/reviews` (`apps/api/src/routes/dealers.ts:125`) returns paginated reviews. Neither endpoint is called anywhere in `apps/web` — `detail-page.tsx`'s dealer info (`OverviewTab.tsx`) only ever shows name/phone/website from the listing scrape itself, never the enriched profile.

`DealerReview.source` is a free-form string; only `"google"` is currently written by any ingestion job. The schema comment lists `"dealerrater"` as an example of a second possible source, but no ingestion code writes it — so today the honest answer to "where does this data come from" is Google Places API only. (Apple has no public ratings API for third-party consumption; Yelp's Fusion API is a candidate for a future source but is out of scope here — this issue is "surface what we already collect," not "collect from a new provider.")

## Problem / Goal

Add a dealer reputation section to the vehicle detail page (likely `WavTab.tsx` or `OverviewTab.tsx`, next to the existing dealer name/phone/website block) showing rating, review count, open/closed-from-hours, and a handful of review snippets — using data that is already collected and already has API routes, just needs a fetch + component.

## Proposed approach

- Add a `getDealerProfile(id)` fetcher in `detail-page.tsx` calling `GET /v1/listings/:id/dealer` (mirrors the existing `getSafety`/`getMarketPricing` pattern), and thread `dealerProfile` into whichever tab renders dealer info.
- Add a `getDealerReviews(dealerId)` fetcher calling `GET /v1/dealers/:id/reviews` (skip a lazy-load-more pattern for v1 — first page, e.g. `take=5`, is enough).
- New small component (e.g. `DealerReputation.tsx`) rendering: star rating + review count, an "open now" derivation from `hours` (already stored as opening-hours JSON from Places), and review cards (author, stars, snippet, relative date, source label).
- Handle the common case gracefully: many listings won't have a matched `DealerProfile` (private sellers, dealers Places couldn't match, or enrichment not yet run) — render nothing or a minimal placeholder, not an error state.
- `DealerReview.text` is third-party user content pulled from Google — no additional sanitization concerns beyond normal text escaping (React already escapes), but keep review snippets truncated/clamped rather than full-length.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A listing whose dealer has an enriched `DealerProfile` with `rating`/`reviewCount` set shows a star rating and review count on the vehicle detail page.
- [ ] The same listing shows at least one review (author, rating, snippet, date) sourced from `GET /v1/dealers/:id/reviews`.
- [ ] A listing with no matched `DealerProfile` (or a private-seller listing) renders the page without error and without an empty/broken dealer-reputation section.
- [ ] Manual QA: load a real dealer listing with enrichment data in dev and confirm ratings/reviews render correctly on both light and dark theme.

## Notes
Source attribution ("via Google") should be shown per-review since `DealerReview.source` already carries it — don't hardcode a Google-only assumption in copy even though it's the only populated source today.

records.title: feat(ops): named template views (perspectives) for the docked-terminal workspace
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): named template views (perspectives) for the docked-terminal workspace
records.issueBody:
## Context

Follow-up idea from the #913 (docked-terminal) design conversation: instead of only opening panels one at a time via nav clicks, let an operator jump straight to a curated layout — e.g. a "Triage" view that docks Problems + Logs together, or a "Health check" view that docks Readiness + Sources — in one action. Think Eclipse-style "perspectives" rather than a new state system: `useWorkspaceState`/`workspace-url.ts` already serialize the full panel set, order, spans, split ratio, and maximized state into the URL (#854), so a "template" is just a named, pre-built URL for that state, not a new architecture.

Deliberately filed separately from #913 rather than folded into it: which layouts are actually worth presetting is only knowable once operators are using the ad-hoc version (#913) day to day. Building presets before that exists risks guessing wrong.

## Problem / Goal

Add a small set of curated, named workspace layouts to the docked-terminal preview (#913) that an operator can switch to in one click, replacing the current panel set rather than merging with it.

## Proposed approach

- A static config, e.g. `apps/ops/src/app/ops/preview/docked-terminal/templates.ts`, listing named templates as plain data: `{ name: string, panels: Array<{ entityType, entityId, span }>, splitRatio?: number }`. Start with 2-3 templates informed by real workflows already in the codebase (e.g. "Triage" ≈ problems + logs, mirroring the drill-down #761 already built; "Health check" ≈ readiness + sources).
- A "Templates" dropdown in the docked-terminal route's header (alongside the status strip discussed in #913) lists these by name; selecting one serializes the template's panel list through the existing `workspace-url.ts` encoding and replaces the current URL/workspace state in one step (not additive — switching templates is a full swap, matching the "perspective switch" mental model, not a merge with whatever's already open).
- No template *authoring* UI in this iteration — templates are developer-defined config, not operator-saved. Operator-saved custom templates (rename/save current layout) is explicitly out of scope here and would be its own follow-up if presets prove useful.
- Depends on #913 shipping first (needs its route, panel set, and URL-state wiring to exist).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At least two named templates are selectable from a "Templates" control on the docked-terminal route, each opening its predefined panel set with its predefined spans.
- [ ] Selecting a template fully replaces the currently open panel set (any panels open before selection are closed, not merged), verified by a component test.
- [ ] The resulting URL after selecting a template matches the URL you'd get by manually opening that same panel set — i.e. templates reuse the existing URL-state contract rather than introducing a parallel one (test asserting URL equivalence).
- [ ] Manual QA: load the docked-terminal route, select each template, confirm the expected panels open with expected spans, reload, and confirm the same template state reproduces from the URL.

## Notes

Blocked on #913 (needs the route and its panel/entity wiring to exist first). No new persistence or state model — this is entirely a thin layer over #854's existing URL-serialized workspace state. Operator-authored/saved templates are a deliberately deferred follow-up, not part of this issue.

records.title: feat(misc): docked-terminal Overview comparison route as first production Workspace consumer
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): docked-terminal Overview comparison route as first production Workspace consumer
records.issueBody:
## Context

Sibling issue to #912 ("dashboard-grid Overview comparison route"): the requester wants two candidate Overview treatments comparable on separate URLs before rebuilding `apps/ops/src/app/ops/OpsOverviewClient.tsx`. This issue is the "docked terminal" candidate — fixed docked panes with a live problems feed and queue diagnostics, panels mounting/unmounting as the operator opens and closes them, rather than one static page.

That capability already exists and is unused: `apps/ops/src/components/Workspace` (`WorkspaceGrid`, `WorkspacePanel`, `WorkspaceResizableSplit`, `useWorkspaceState`) implements the full panel contract from #854 — URL-addressable panel identity, grid spans, resizable splits, maximize/restore — but per `apps/ops/src/app/workspace-preview/WorkspacePreviewClient.tsx`'s own comment, "no production route consumes the workspace contract yet." This issue is that first consumer, scoped as a comparison route rather than a change to the real Overview.

Follow-up in conversation established three more requirements: nav clicks should open/focus a panel instead of navigating to a separate page, so information stays "tied together"; panels should link to related entities per #854's existing (but unused) "entity relationship links" contract; and the docked panes' own borders should be adjustable, plus panels should support a collapsed/minimized state, not just open/closed/maximized.

## Problem / Goal

Build a preview route that opens real entity panels (site readiness, active problems feed, queue diagnostics) through the existing `Workspace` components, backed by live data, wired to the left nav, with adjustable pane borders and a minimize state — so panels genuinely open/close/mount on demand and cross-link to each other, and the result can be compared against #912 and the current `/ops`.

## Proposed approach

- New route `apps/ops/src/app/ops/preview/docked-terminal/page.tsx` + `DockedTerminalClient.tsx`, following the `workspace-preview` route's structure (`useWorkspaceState`, `WorkspaceGrid`, `WorkspaceResizableSplit`) but replacing its `DEMO_ENTITIES`/`renderDemoPanel` fixtures with real panels:
  - a `readiness` panel sourced from the same data as `apps/ops/src/app/ops/readiness/ReadinessClient.tsx`;
  - a `problems` panel sourced from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/problems/ProblemsClient.tsx`'s data, rendered as a live-updating feed;
  - a `queues` panel sourced from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/queues/QueuesClient.tsx`, using `WorkspaceResizableSplit` for a queue-list / queue-detail split as the existing preview already demonstrates for the `queue` entity type.
- **Nav wiring**: on this route, `NavColumn`/`NavRail` items that map to one of the above entity types (readiness, problems, queues; sources/runs/schedules/logs if time allows) call `workspace.openPanel(entityType, entityId)` instead of navigating, opening or focusing that panel in the grid. Nav items with no corresponding panel yet (AI provider settings, Bull Board, Field conflicts) keep normal navigation. Route-scoped only — this does not change nav behavior on any other page.
- **Entity relationship links**: within the `problems` panel, a problem tied to a source opens/focuses a `source` panel without closing `problems`; within `queues`, a queue's failed-job count opens/focuses a `logs` panel filtered to that job. Implements the previously-unused "entity relationship links" AC from #854.
- **Adjustable pane borders**: apply `WorkspaceResizableSplit` one level up, between the docked panes themselves (not just within one panel's internal split as today), so the operator can drag to resize the readiness pane against the problems/queues stack.
- **Minimize state**: extend the shared `WorkspacePanel`/`useWorkspaceState` (used by both this route and `workspace-preview`) with a fourth panel state — minimized — alongside the existing open/closed/maximized states: a minimized panel collapses to a title-bar-only strip docked along the bottom edge of the workspace; clicking it restores the panel to its prior span/position.
- Add a thin status strip (live indicator, auto-refresh cadence) below the grid, matching the affordance discussed for the desktop-app feel; new UI, scoped to this route only.
- Gate the route the same way `workspace-preview` is gated today (non-production / operator-only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/ops/preview/docked-terminal` renders live readiness, problems, and queue data through real `WorkspacePanel`s (not the existing route's demo fixtures), using `useWorkspaceState`/`WorkspaceGrid` from #854's contract.
- [ ] Clicking a wired nav item (readiness, problems, or queues) opens or focuses the corresponding panel in the workspace instead of navigating away; nav items with no panel mapping still navigate normally (component/E2E test per item).
- [ ] From the `problems` panel, activating a problem's source link opens/focuses a `source` panel while `problems` stays open; from `queues`, a failed-job count opens/focuses a `logs` panel filtered to that job (component test asserting both panels are open afterward).
- [ ] The divider between the docked panes is draggable and resizes the panes' relative widths, verified by a component test simulating a drag and asserting the resulting layout.
- [ ] A panel can be minimized to a title-bar strip and restored to its prior span/position without losing its content or URL state (component test), extending `WorkspacePanel`'s existing open/closed/maximized states.
- [ ] Closing and reopening a panel actually unmounts/remounts its content (component test spying on mount/unmount), not just visually hiding it.
- [ ] The open panel set, order, span, minimized, and maximized state reproduce on a full reload from the URL alone, consistent with the existing `workspace-preview` route's guarantee.
- [ ] The route is gated the same way `workspace-preview`/`inspector-preview` are today, and does not alter `/ops`, any existing production route, or nav behavior on any page other than this preview route.
- [ ] Manual QA: open `/ops/preview/docked-terminal`, click a wired nav item and confirm it opens a panel rather than navigating, follow an entity relationship link, drag the pane divider, minimize and restore a panel, reload, and confirm state and data all reproduce correctly.

## Notes

Does not change `/ops/workspace-preview` (kept as the generic dev harness, though it inherits the new minimized state for free since that lives in the shared `WorkspacePanel`) or the real Overview. See #912 for the dashboard-grid candidate being compared against this one — that route intentionally does *not* get nav-wiring, entity links, or resizable borders, since it's evaluating a different, non-panel-based layout philosophy. A follow-up issue after a direction is picked would migrate the winner into `OpsOverviewClient.tsx` and remove the losing preview route (and, if docked-terminal wins, close out #854's "no production route consumes the workspace contract yet" gap directly).

records.title: feat(ops): add dashboard-grid Overview comparison preview route
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): dashboard-grid Overview comparison route (widget panels over existing data)
records.issueBody:
## Context

Feedback on the ops app: the Overview reads as "a list of links to pages" rather than a command-center home. The requester wants to compare two concrete Overview treatments side by side, on separate URLs, before committing to a rebuild of `apps/ops/src/app/ops/OpsOverviewClient.tsx`. This issue is the "dashboard grid" candidate; the sibling issue #913 (docked-terminal / Workspace panels) is the other candidate — they're deliberately independent so both can be reviewed live rather than argued over mockups.

A design-lead prototype was built and reviewed in conversation (not committed) showing the shape: a CSS grid of dense, data-forward widget panels (Service health, Active problems, Queue depth, Recent source runs, Recurring jobs, Site readiness-as-checklist) instead of today's link list.

Follow-up in conversation: panels should be adjustable, but as **preset size options chosen from a per-panel menu** (Apple Home-screen-widget style — Small/Medium/Large), not freehand drag-resize. Freehand drag-resize was explicitly listed as a non-goal for the first iteration in the ratified #851 architecture decision ("Providing a fully arbitrary draggable dashboard"); presets stay inside that boundary. Panels should also be collapsible (to a title-bar-only strip) or closable outright.

## Problem / Goal

Add a new dev-facing preview route that renders the *existing* Overview data (no new API surface) as a grid of independent widget panels with per-panel size-preset, collapse, and close controls, so it can be compared against the current `/ops` Overview and the docked-terminal candidate (#913).

## Proposed approach

- New route `apps/ops/src/app/ops/preview/dashboard-grid/page.tsx` + `DashboardGridClient.tsx`, wrapped in `OpsShell`/`OpsNav` like other routes (see `apps/ops/src/app/ops/problems/page.tsx` for the current pattern).
- Reuse existing data-fetching, not new endpoints: the health/status fetch already in `OpsOverviewClient.tsx`, the problems list from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/problems/ProblemsClient.tsx`'s data source, queue depth from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/queues/QueuesClient.tsx`, recent runs from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/runs/RunsClient.tsx`, schedules from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/schedules/SchedulesClient.tsx`, and readiness checks from `apps/ops/src/app/ops/readiness/ReadinessClient.tsx`.
- A local `GridPanel` component (route-local, not the shared `Workspace` package — this route deliberately doesn't use entity-panel semantics) renders each section with:
  - a top-right menu button offering **Small / Medium / Large** presets, each mapping to a fixed grid column/row span (e.g. Small = 1 col, Medium = 2 col, Large = 2 col × 2 row);
  - a collapse control that shrinks the panel to its title bar only (content unmounted, header remains, still occupying its grid cell at minimum height);
  - a close control that removes the panel from the grid entirely for the session.
- Size/collapsed/closed choices are session-only (component state, reset on reload) in this iteration — no persistence requirement, since this is a comparison route, not the real Overview.
- The site-readiness panel renders as a dense multi-column checklist (narrower rows than the current `/ops/readiness` page), addressing the original "rows are too wide" feedback.
- Gate the route so it's reachable only in non-production builds or behind an operator-only flag, consistent with how `workspace-preview`/`inspector-preview` are gated today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/ops/preview/dashboard-grid` renders live data (not fixtures) for service health, active problems, queue depth, recent source runs, recurring jobs, and site readiness, each as a distinct `GridPanel`.
- [ ] Each panel's menu offers Small/Medium/Large size presets, and selecting one changes the panel's grid column/row span immediately (component test asserting the applied span per preset).
- [ ] Each panel can be collapsed to a title-bar-only strip (content unmounts) and expanded again, and closed entirely (removed from the grid) — verified by component tests.
- [ ] The site-readiness panel renders as a dense multi-column checklist (narrower rows than `/ops/readiness`), verified by a component test asserting the row/column structure.
- [ ] The route is unreachable in a production build the same way `workspace-preview`/`inspector-preview` are gated, and does not change any existing `/ops` route's behavior.
- [ ] Manual QA: open `/ops/preview/dashboard-grid`, cycle each panel through its size presets, collapse one, close another, reload and confirm the page still matches current data, and confirm every panel's data matches its equivalent current page (health, problems, queues, runs, schedules, readiness).

## Notes

Deliberately does not touch `/ops` (the real Overview) or `apps/ops/src/app/ops/OpsOverviewClient.tsx` — this is a side-by-side comparison route only. Deliberately does not add freehand drag-resize (see Context) — if that's wanted later, it needs its own decision revisiting #851's non-goal, not silent scope creep here. A follow-up issue (filed after a direction is chosen) would migrate the winning layout into the real Overview and delete whichever preview route loses. See #913 for the Workspace-panel ("docked terminal") candidate.

records.title: feat(ops): collapsible, reopenable icon rail for the desktop NavColumn
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): collapsible, reopenable icon rail for the desktop NavColumn
records.issueBody:
## Context

Feedback on the current ops nav (\`apps/ops/src/components/OpsNav\`): at ≥1024px, \`OpsNav.tsx\` renders \`NavColumn\` unconditionally — a full labeled column with no way to collapse it. The 768–1023px \`NavRail\` (icon-only) and the ≤767px \`MobileNav\` are pure CSS breakpoint swaps with no user control at all. There is no toggle anywhere in the shell to shrink the desktop column down to icons, unlike e.g. VS Code's sidebar collapse. Confirmed via \`git log --follow -- apps/ops/src/components/OpsNav/OpsNav.tsx\`: the responsive nav shipped whole-cloth in #730 with no collapse affordance at any point.

## Problem / Goal

Add a user-controlled collapse/expand toggle to the desktop (≥1024px) nav column in \`NavColumn.tsx\`, so an operator can shrink it to an icon rail and reopen it, with the choice persisted across reloads.

## Proposed approach

- Add a toggle button at the top of \`NavColumn.tsx\` (mirrors the collapse chevron used in the command-center prototype) that flips a `collapsed` boolean.
- Persist the boolean in `localStorage` (a small hook alongside the existing `apps/ops/src/components/OpsNav/useViewTransitionNav.ts` pattern), read on mount to avoid a flash of the wrong state.
- When collapsed, render icon-only rows reusing `NavRail.tsx`'s icon markup/`nav-icons.ts` rather than duplicating icon SVGs, with each item's `title` as a native tooltip and an accessible name preserved for screen readers.
- Keep `NavRail` (768–1023px) and `MobileNav` (≤767px) untouched — this only affects the ≥1024px `NavColumn` breakpoint.
- The toggle button itself remains visible and reachable in both collapsed and expanded states.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At ≥1024px, clicking the toggle collapses `NavColumn` to icon-only width and clicking it again reopens the full labeled column; the current state exposes an accessible name (e.g. "Collapse navigation" / "Expand navigation").
- [ ] The collapsed/expanded choice persists across a full page reload (test asserts `localStorage` is read on mount and the correct width/markup renders immediately).
- [ ] Every nav item remains keyboard-focusable and its accessible name is unchanged in both states (existing `NavColumn.test.tsx` / `NavRail.test.tsx` coverage extended, not just relying on `title` attributes).
- [ ] Manual QA: at a ≥1024px viewport, toggle collapse/expand, reload while collapsed, and confirm the icon rail state survives the reload and every icon still opens its route.

## Notes

Prototype reference discussed in-conversation (not committed to the repo): a rail toggle button at the top of the nav flips between icon-only and icon+label, matching the mental model of VS Code's sidebar collapse. Independent of the two Overview-layout comparison issues filed alongside this one; no shared files.
