records.title: fix(web): resolve client API host at runtime instead of build time
records.issueTitle: bug(deploy): production web images never receive a real NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL at build time
records.issueBody:
## Problem

Discovered while root-causing the current CI E2E instability (#815). `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env vars are inlined into the Next.js client bundle at `next build` time, not read from the container's runtime environment. Several `apps/web` client components (`CategoryBarChart.tsx`, and the histogram components per #830's own notes) reference `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` directly in `'use client'` files, so only a build-time value reaches them — a runtime `environment:` entry in compose is silently inert for this specific value.

`docker/web.Dockerfile` never declared `ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` (only the Sentry vars), so every `next build` — including the one run by the "Docker build (web)" CI matrix job that produces the images `publish` pushes to GHCR — has always run with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` unset, baking in `apps/web/src/lib/api-url.ts`'s `DEFAULT_PUBLIC_API_URL` fallback (`http://localhost:3001` before #830, `http://localhost:4001` after).

`docker-compose.prod.yml` requires operators to set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` at deploy time (`${NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL:?set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}`), but that only reaches the server process — the already-built, already-published image's client bundle has `localhost:...` permanently baked in regardless. In any real deployed environment, `localhost` inside a visitor's own browser never reaches the API. This means every client-fetched widget on `apps/web` — the Discover/results facet groups (`CategoryBarChart`), the state heat map, and the price/mileage/year histograms — has likely never worked against a real deployed API, only appearing to work in local dev where `localhost` happens to be correct by coincidence.

## Root cause

Same class of bug fixed narrowly for CI/E2E in #815 (docker/web.Dockerfile now declares `ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` and CI's E2E-job build step / docker-compose.yml / e2e/docker-compose.e2e.yml now pass a matching build-arg) — but the "Docker build (web)" CI matrix job that produces the images `publish` actually ships to GHCR still passes no `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` build-arg at all, because there is no single correct value at that stage: production's real public API URL is deploy-target-specific and isn't known when a shared, once-per-commit image is built.

## Proposed approaches (needs a decision, not prescribing one)

- Build the web image per deployment target with the correct `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` baked in (loses the current "build once, promote everywhere" digest-pinning model `publish` relies on), or
- Refactor the affected client components to stop reading `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` directly and instead go through a same-origin proxy/BFF route, the way `apps/ops` already does via `/api/bff` (`apps/ops/src/lib/api-url.ts`) — this removes the build-time/runtime split entirely, or
- Inject the API URL at container start via a small runtime script that rewrites a placeholder in the already-built static/client assets (a known Next.js pattern for this exact problem).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide and document the chosen approach (BFF proxy vs. per-target build vs. runtime injection).
- [ ] Confirm whether any real deployed environment exists today and, if so, audit whether Discover facets / state heat map / histograms have actually been broken in it.
- [ ] Client-fetched widgets in `apps/web` resolve the real API host in a built, published production image without requiring a rebuild per environment (unless that is the chosen approach).
- [ ] Regression coverage: a test (unit, integration, or E2E) that would have caught `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` silently falling back to `localhost` in a built image.

## References

- #815 (CI stabilization — where this was found)
- #830 (changed the `localhost` fallback value, which is what made the pre-existing bug newly visible in CI)

records.title: ops/ai: auto-download Ollama models with pull progress UI
records.issueTitle: ops/ai: auto-download Ollama models with pull progress UI
records.issueBody:
## Background

The ops/ai model configuration page lets operators pick which Ollama model to use per AI job. When a model that isn't yet installed is selected, the Ollama `/api/generate` call will fail silently. A pull/download flow would make it easy to install models directly from the UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A **Pull** or **Download** button appears next to any model that is in the catalog but not yet installed on the connected Ollama instance
- [ ] Clicking Pull calls a Next.js API route that proxies `POST /api/pull` from Ollama (which streams newline-delimited JSON progress events)
- [ ] The UI shows live pull progress: layer download percentages and a completion indicator
- [ ] On success, the installed model list refreshes automatically and the model is marked as installed
- [ ] On failure, a clear error message is shown (model not found, Ollama unreachable, etc.)
- [ ] No page reload required — the whole flow is in-place

## Technical notes

- Ollama pull endpoint: `POST ${OLLAMA_BASE_URL}/api/pull` with `{ name: model, stream: true }`
- Response: newline-delimited JSON, each line is `{ status, digest, total, completed }` or `{ status: "success" }`
- Next.js API route can use `ReadableStream` / `TransformStream` to proxy the Ollama stream to the browser as SSE or raw NDJSON
- The client reads the stream with `fetch` + `ReadableStream` and updates progress state per layer
- Scope: only on the ops/ai page — not on the home page or intake flow

## Scope / out of scope

In scope: pull/download from the ops/ai model config table
Out of scope: auto-pull on model selection save (too surprising), pushing to production Ollama instances

## Problem

Creating a new listing with a non-null price can fail with:

`Invalid prisma.listing.create() invocation: Foreign key constraint violated on the constraint: listing_price_history_listingId_fkey`

The create path currently uses nested `priceHistory.create` under `listing.create`, making the child row implicit and harder to diagnose when the parent listing write is not visible as expected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New listing ingestion creates the parent listing before inserting initial price, mileage, and conversion history rows.
- [ ] History rows use the created listing id explicitly and remain in the same transaction.
- [ ] Re-ingesting the same listing remains idempotent and does not duplicate history rows.
- [ ] Existing update-path behavior still writes history only when values change.
- [ ] Tests cover the new create-path ordering and existing update-path behavior.

records.title: feat(ops): show/hide toggle for password field on login page
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): show/hide toggle for password field on login page
records.issueBody:
## Context
While debugging a local `make dev` login failure (empty `OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`), it became clear the ops login form has no way to verify what was actually typed into the password field — the standard browser-native masking made a blank/typo'd password hard to distinguish from a correct one.

## Problem / Goal
Add a show/hide toggle to the password field on the ops login page (`apps/ops/src/app/login/LoginForm.tsx`) so operators can visually confirm their input before submitting.

## Proposed approach
- `apps/ops/src/app/login/LoginForm.tsx`: wrap the password `<input>` in a relatively-positioned container; add a `type="button"` toggle (not part of tab order, `tabIndex={-1}`, so Enter still submits) that flips the input's `type` between `password` and `text`, using `Eye`/`EyeOff` icons from the existing `lucide-react` dependency. Mirror the icon-button accessibility pattern (`aria-label`, `title`) from `apps/ops/src/components/CopyButton.tsx`.
- `apps/ops/src/app/login/page.module.css`: absolutely position the toggle button inside the input's box on the right side, with `padding-right` on the input so typed text doesn't run under the icon.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking the eye icon toggles the password input between masked (`type="password"`) and revealed (`type="text"`) without submitting the form or losing focus/cursor position.
- [ ] The icon button has an `aria-label` that reflects its current action ("Show password" / "Hide password") and is excluded from tab order so keyboard users reach "Sign in" directly after the password field.
- [ ] Manual QA: on `/login`, visually confirm the icon sits inside the password field (not as a separate adjacent element) and matches the app's existing dark theme styling in both default and hover/focus states.

## Notes
Related to the same debugging session that fixed the empty `OPS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` env var causing all logins to fail (no tracked code change — local `.env.local` only).

records.title: Fix dev CSP eval error with Next.js Turbopack
records.issueTitle: Fix dev CSP eval error with Next.js Turbopack
records.issueBody:
## Problem

When running the local dev stack and opening the ops app, the browser console reports:

```text
Error Type: Console Error
Error Message: eval() is not supported in this environment. If this page was served with a Content-Security-Policy header, make sure that unsafe-eval is included. React requires eval() in development mode for various debugging features like reconstructing callstacks from a different environment.
React will never use eval() in production mode

Next.js version: 16.2.10 (Turbopack)
```

This appears to be a local-development-only CSP incompatibility: React/Next development mode needs eval-like behavior for debugging, while the served CSP blocks it.

## Context

- Local dev command: `make dev`
- Ops dev URL: `http://localhost:4002`
- Next.js: `16.2.10`
- Bundler: Turbopack
- Production should continue to avoid `unsafe-eval`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Opening the ops app in local development no longer emits the React/Next `eval() is not supported` console error.
- [ ] The fix is scoped to development mode only, or otherwise preserves the production CSP posture without `unsafe-eval`.
- [ ] Any shared CSP helper/config has tests or targeted coverage proving dev and production directives differ as intended.
- [ ] If the dev URL documentation is touched, `docs/ops/quick-start.md` reflects the current `make dev` ops URL.

## Done when

- [ ] `make dev` serves the ops app successfully at `http://localhost:4002` without this console error.
- [ ] Relevant checks pass, at minimum `pnpm check:affected`.

records.title: fix(web): standardize sort dropdown labels and add reverse-direction options
records.issueTitle: feat(web): standardize and expand sort dropdown labels/options
records.issueBody:
## Context
The search results sort dropdown (`apps/web/src/components/SearchFilters.tsx`, `SearchFilters.sortOptions` in `messages/en.json`/`es.json`/`zz.json`) has inconsistent label casing and phrasing ("Low to high" vs "Newest first" vs "Lowest mileage"), includes marketing copy ("by WAV Search") in a functional control, and is missing the reverse direction for two of its three numeric/date fields (no "high mileage first", no "oldest year first", no "oldest found first").

## Problem / Goal
Standardize every sort label to a consistent `Category: Direction` format and add the missing reverse-direction options, so the dropdown is predictable and complete. Backend confirmed to accept arbitrary `field:direction` strings (`apps/api/src/services/listing-search.ts:116`, `apps/api/src/routes/listings.ts:221`) with no allowlist, so no backend validation changes are required — only the frontend option list/values and translation strings change.

Rename/add mapping (label → provider sort value):
- `newestListings`: "Recently found by WAV Search" → **"Date Found: New to Old"** (`listedAt:desc`, unchanged value, default)
- NEW: **"Date Found: Old to New"** (`listedAt:asc`)
- `priceLowToHigh`: "Price: Low to high" → **"Price: Low to High"** (`priceCents:asc`, unchanged value)
- `priceHighToLow`: "Price: High to low" → **"Price: High to Low"** (`priceCents:desc`, unchanged value)
- `lowestMileage`: "Lowest mileage" → **"Mileage: Low to High"** (`mileage:asc`, unchanged value)
- NEW: **"Mileage: High to Low"** (`mileage:desc`)
- `yearNewestFirst`: "Year: Newest first" → **"Year: New to Old"** (`year:desc`, unchanged value)
- NEW: **"Year: Old to New"** (`year:asc`)

## Proposed approach
- Update `sortOptions` keys/strings in `apps/web/messages/en.json`, `es.json` (translate), and `zz.json` (pseudo-locale) — rename existing keys to match new copy and add 3 new keys for the new reverse-direction options.
- Update `apps/web/src/components/SearchFilters.tsx` `<option>` list: reorder into paired groups (Date Found / Price / Mileage / Year, each New-to-Old or Low-to-High first), wire the 3 new `<option value=...>` entries to the new translation keys.
- Confirm the default sort (`listedAt:desc`) is unaffected in `SearchFilters.tsx` (client default) and `apps/web/src/app/[locale]/filters/page.tsx` (server default).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sort dropdown renders exactly 8 options in the order: Date Found (New to Old, Old to New), Price (Low to High, High to Low), Mileage (Low to High, High to Low), Year (New to Old, Old to New)
- [ ] No option label contains "by WAV Search" or inconsistent casing ("to high"/"to low"/"first")
- [ ] Selecting "Mileage: High to Low", "Year: Old to New", or "Date Found: Old to New" updates the results list and URL `sort` param to `mileage:desc`, `year:asc`, and `listedAt:asc` respectively
- [ ] es.json and zz.json sortOptions blocks updated in parallel with en.json (no missing-translation console warnings)
- [ ] Manual QA: on `/[locale]/filters`, open the sort dropdown and verify all 8 labels read correctly and each produces correctly ordered results (spot-check price and year directions)

## Notes
Backend already supports arbitrary `field:direction` sort expressions with no allowlist — verified via `apps/api/src/services/listing-search.ts:116` and `apps/api/src/routes/listings.ts:221`. No API changes required.

records.title: feat(ops): /ops/problems surface + overview Attention-panel slimming (fixes #892)
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): /ops/problems surface + overview Attention-panel slimming (#758)
records.issueBody:
## Context

Child issue of #758 (unified problem triage). Per #758's disposition on #851 (`docs/design/ui-boundary-and-ops-workspace.md` section 5) and the migration order in section 7, this UI work is **blocked on #854** (Ops workspace/panel contract) — the Problems surface must consume the same panel/entity conventions #854 defines rather than building a second, incompatible detail system. Do not start until #854 lands.

The backend this page renders from is #890 (problem aggregation) and #891 (acknowledgement persistence) — both UI-independent and can proceed/complete first.

## Problem / Goal

Add a `/ops/problems` route listing active problems ranked by severity and recency (first-seen, last-seen, occurrence count, severity, deep link to the fix surface), with operator acknowledge/unacknowledge. Slim the overview's Attention panel to a count + top-N preview linking to this page, replacing its current full recompute (`apps/ops/src/app/ops/overview-helpers.ts` / `OpsOverviewClient.tsx`) with a call to the same server-side aggregate.

## Proposed approach

- Build `/ops/problems` using the panel/entity conventions from #854 (built on `@wivwav/ui-web`), not a bespoke layout.
- Consume #890's aggregation route and #891's ack route.
- Overview Attention panel: replace its current logic with a small count + top-N preview backed by the same aggregate call, linking through to `/ops/problems`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/ops/problems` shows every active problem's first-seen, last-seen, occurrence count, severity, and a working deep link to its fix surface.
- [ ] Acknowledging a problem removes it from the default view without deleting its history; an "acknowledged" filter/toggle can still surface it.
- [ ] The overview Attention panel and `/ops/problems` render from the same aggregation call (#890) — no forked computation — verified by a test.
- [ ] Manual QA: exercise `/ops/problems` and the overview preview on a narrow (mobile-width) viewport and a desktop viewport per #854's workspace conventions.

Blocked on #854. Do not begin implementation before #854 merges — see #758's pre-implementation agreement comment and the #851 decision record section 7 migration order.

records.title: chore(agents): tighten worker.md commit-granularity guidance (fixes #896)
records.issueTitle: chore(agents): tighten worker.md commit-granularity guidance to require per-layer commits
records.issueBody:
## Context
#686 added "commit after each coherent functional slice; avoid WIP commits and unrelated churn" to worker.md, but in practice workers treat the entire issue as one slice. Recent history shows one commit per issue rather than several: #761 (13 files, +600), #797 (7 files, +728), #798 (10 files, +754), #852 spike (23 files, +3246). The repo's merge queue uses REBASE (not squash), so this is not a post-merge squash artifact — it's exactly what workers commit.

## Problem / Goal
`.claude/roles/worker.md` step 8 is descriptive ("coherent functional slice") rather than prescriptive, leaving slice size to worker judgment. Tighten it to name concrete commit boundaries so multi-layer issues produce multiple commits instead of one.

## Proposed approach
Edit `.claude/roles/worker.md` step 8 to require separate commits per logical layer touched by an issue, e.g.: schema/migration, then service/business logic, then API/route wiring, then UI, then tests-with-behavior (tests may ride with the behavior they cover rather than as a separate trailing commit). Keep wording terse per #686's note ("prefer 'coherent' over vague 'small' wording") while making the layer boundaries explicit enough that a worker can mechanically apply them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.claude/roles/worker.md` step 8 names concrete commit boundaries (schema/migration, service logic, API wiring, UI, tests-with-behavior) instead of only "coherent functional slice."
- [ ] Wording stays terse (comparable length to the current step) and preserves the existing WIP/unrelated-churn prohibition.
- [ ] A single-layer issue (e.g. a CSS-only fix) is not forced into artificial multi-commit splitting — the guidance only requires splitting when an issue actually spans multiple layers.

## Notes
Follow-up to #686. Not a squash-artifact issue — merge queue `merge_method` is `REBASE`, confirmed via `docs/design/merge-queue.md`.

records.title: feat(api): operator acknowledgement + first-seen/last-seen persistence for aggregated problems (#758)
records.issueTitle: feat(api): operator acknowledgement + first-seen/last-seen persistence for aggregated problems (#758)
records.issueBody:
## Context

Child issue of #758 (unified problem triage), sibling to #890 (problem aggregation). Pre-implementation agreement on #758 defines the persistence boundary: the only state with no home in an existing external tool is operator acknowledgement, plus first-seen/last-seen/occurrence tracking for domain-sourced problems (which have no native history — `computeAttentionSnapshot` recomputes fresh every call). Server-side; UI-independent; unblocked while #854 is pending.

## Problem / Goal

Add a single persistence table, `ops_problem_state`, keyed by the `fingerprint` scheme from #758/#890, and an admin route to acknowledge/unacknowledge a problem by fingerprint.

## Proposed approach

- New migration adding `ops_problem_state`: `fingerprint` (PK, text), `source` (`domain` | `grafana` | `sentry`), `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at`, `occurrence_count`, `acknowledged_at` (nullable), `acknowledged_by` (nullable).
- A per-aggregation-pass upsert (called from wherever #890's aggregate is invoked, e.g. on each `/admin/problem-aggregate` request or a lightweight scheduled pass — implementer's call, document the choice): for every fingerprint present in the current pass, set `last_seen_at = now`, increment `occurrence_count`, and set `first_seen_at = now` only if the row doesn't already exist. Rows are never deleted so ack history survives a flapping condition; a fingerprint absent from N consecutive passes is simply not "active" (definition of N is this issue's call, document it).
- For `source = 'grafana'` / `'sentry'` rows, `first_seen_at`/`last_seen_at`/`occurrence_count` in this table are informational only (#890's live-federated values from Grafana/Sentry's own APIs are authoritative for display) — only `acknowledged_at`/`acknowledged_by` are authoritative from this table regardless of source.
- New admin route (e.g. `apps/api/src/routes/admin-problem-ack.ts`) with POST to acknowledge/unacknowledge a fingerprint, following the existing `admin-attention.ts`/`admin-logs.ts` route-plugin conventions (auth, validation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Migration creates `ops_problem_state` with the columns above; a repeated upsert for the same fingerprint updates `last_seen_at`/`occurrence_count` without resetting `first_seen_at`, verified by a test.
- [ ] Acknowledge/unacknowledge route round-trips: acknowledging a fingerprint persists `acknowledged_at`/`acknowledged_by`, unacknowledging clears them, verified by route-level tests.
- [ ] Acknowledged state persists independently of whether the problem is still active in the current aggregation pass (i.e. acking a since-resolved domain condition doesn't error or get silently dropped).

## Notes

Depends on #890 for the fingerprint scheme (do not diverge from it). The `/ops/problems` UI that surfaces ack/unack to operators remains blocked on #854 per #758 — this issue is the persistence layer only.

records.title: feat(ops): define and implement the Ops workspace/panel contract
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): define and implement the Ops workspace/panel contract
records.issueBody:
## Context

Implements the Ops workspace contract from `docs/design/ui-boundary-and-ops-workspace.md`
section 3, decided in #851. Adapts the existing `apps/ops/src/components/Inspector`
(the E6 inspector #761 already extends) rather than replacing it outright.
Depends on #853's foundation package.

## Problem / Goal

Give Ops a dynamic workspace that can open contextual entity panels, span
them across grid columns, resize or maximize a panel, and preserve deep
links — without a bespoke layout system per screen.

## Proposed approach

- Panel identity keyed as `{entityType}:{entityId}`; opening an already-open
  panel focuses it.
- Full open-panel set, order, spans, and maximized state serialize into the
  URL.
- CSS Grid for column spans; one focused split/resize dependency only where
  operator-controlled resizing is needed; no drag/drop repositioning yet.
- Maximize/restore as a workspace layout mode (not a modal): background stays
  in the tab order, Escape restores, state lives in the URL, focus moves to
  the panel heading on both transitions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Panels have a stable, URL-addressable ID of the form `{entityType}:{entityId}`; opening an already-open panel focuses it instead of duplicating it.
- [ ] Entity relationship links between panels open or focus the related panel without closing the current one.
- [ ] The full open-panel set, order, spans, and maximized state serialize into the URL, reproducing the exact workspace on reload/share.
- [ ] Panels lay out via CSS Grid with declarable column spans (1, 2, full-width); no arbitrary drag/drop repositioning in this iteration.
- [ ] A resizable split is available only where operator-controlled resizing is needed, via one focused split/resize dependency.
- [ ] Maximize/restore is implemented as a workspace layout mode, not a modal dialog: background content stays in the tab order, Escape restores the previous layout, maximized state is part of URL state, and focus moves to the panel's heading on both maximize and restore.
- [ ] Each panel owns its own internal scroll region; the workspace shell does not scroll horizontally.
- [ ] Panels are accessible landmark regions with accessible names derived from entity identity; open/close/focus/maximize/restore are keyboard-operable; entity actions are exposed via visible buttons, an overflow menu, and a keyboard-accessible context menu.
- [ ] Below the mobile-first breakpoint, panels stack to a single column and open as a full-screen view rather than a small tile.
- [ ] Test coverage is split across package unit tests, Storybook interaction/accessibility/visual tests, `apps/ops` integration tests, and Playwright e2e per the test-strategy table in the decision record — without duplicating vendor component tests.
- [ ] Manual QA: exercise the workspace on a narrow (mobile-width) viewport and a desktop viewport, confirming panel stacking, keyboard operability, and deep-link reload all work as specified.

## Notes

Depends on #853. #761's run/source/queue/log drill-down is intended to
become the first production consumer of this contract, tracked separately in
#761 and not duplicated here.

records.title: feat(api): federate domain conditions, Grafana alerts, and Sentry issues (#890)
records.issueTitle: feat(api): federate domain conditions, Grafana alerts, and Sentry issues into a problem aggregate (#758)
records.issueBody:
## Context

Child issue of #758 (unified problem triage). Pre-implementation agreement recorded on #758 defines the fingerprint scheme, federation/persistence boundary, and shared snapshot seam this issue implements. Server-side; UI-independent; unblocked while #854 (Ops workspace/panel contract) is still pending — see #758's disposition in `docs/design/ui-boundary-and-ops-workspace.md` section 5.

## Problem / Goal

Build the problem-aggregation computation that federates three sources into one typed list of "problems": the shared domain snapshot (`computeAttentionSnapshot` in `apps/api/src/domain/attention-snapshot.ts`, from #774), Grafana alert-instance state (`docker/grafana/provisioning/alerting/wivwav-alert-rules.yaml`), and Sentry issue summaries. No new domain-condition logic — this only federates and fingerprints existing signal.

## Proposed approach

- New pure function `computeProblemAggregate(...)` alongside `attention-snapshot.ts` (e.g. `apps/api/src/domain/problem-aggregate.ts`) that takes already-fetched inputs (same "caller reports state, function never fetches" pattern as `computeAttentionSnapshot`) and returns typed `Problem[]` with: `fingerprint`, `source`, `severity`, `detail`, `evidenceId`/deep-link, plus live-federated `firstSeen`/`lastSeen`/`occurrenceCount` where the source tracks it.
- Fingerprints: `domain:${code}:${evidenceId}` (reuse `AttentionCondition.code`/`evidenceId` from #774 directly), `grafana:${rule.uid}`, `sentry:${issue.id}` — as agreed on #758.
- New read-only server routes to fetch Grafana alert-instance state and Sentry issue summaries (new `apps/api/src/routes/admin-grafana-alerts.ts` and `admin-sentry-issues.ts`, or combined — implementer's call), following the existing `admin-attention.ts` route-plugin pattern. Sentry call needs `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`/`SENTRY_ORG` available server-side in `apps/api` (currently only configured for `apps/web`'s build-time source-map upload) — add read-only API-side env vars, do not reuse the build-time token if scopes differ.
- Both external calls must degrade gracefully: an unreachable Grafana or Sentry contributes zero problems from that source and is reported as unavailable in the aggregate's availability summary, mirroring `signalAvailability` in `attention-snapshot.ts`. Never throw.
- No persistence in this issue — acknowledgement storage is a separate child issue (see #758). This issue's output is the live-federated list only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `computeProblemAggregate` (or equivalently named pure function) unit-tested with fixtures covering: all sources available, each source individually unavailable, zero problems, and fingerprint stability across two calls with unchanged input.
- [ ] Domain conditions in the aggregate come from `computeAttentionSnapshot` directly (no duplicated condition logic) — verified by a test asserting the same condition produces the same fingerprint/detail in both the ops overview path and this aggregate.
- [ ] New Grafana and Sentry read routes return typed, unavailable-safe responses and have route-level tests covering the unreachable-backend case (mocked).
- [ ] Aggregating with Grafana or Sentry unreachable still returns the domain-sourced problems and marks the unreachable source explicitly, verified by a test.

## Notes

Persistence (ack state, first-seen/last-seen for domain-only problems) is intentionally out of scope here — see the sibling child issue. The `/ops/problems` UI and overview slimming remain blocked on #854 per #758.

records.title: feat(ops): legibility pass — sans-serif UI text, monospace reserved for data
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): legibility pass — sans-serif UI text, monospace reserved for data
records.issueBody:
## Context

The ops app's base body font is monospace: `globals.css` sets `body { font-family: var(--font) }` where `--font` is the mono token, and every one of the 11 theme pairs in `apps/ops/src/styles/themes.css` maps `--font` to a monospace face. The default theme ("terminal", set in `apps/ops/src/app/layout.tsx`) renders body text in JetBrains Mono with Rajdhani — a condensed squarish display face — for headings. Reading prose, labels, and table text in monospace at 14 px is fatiguing, and several themes are effectively novelty (VT323 is a CRT pixel font; "hacker"/"matrix" use a single display/mono face for everything including prose).

The requester's feedback: "the font choice sucks." This is a legibility problem, not a taste problem: mono earns its keep for data alignment, not for sentences.

## Problem / Goal

Invert the typographic default: UI text (headings, labels, prose, table text, buttons, nav) renders in each theme's sans face (`--font-ui`); monospace (`--font`) is reserved for data values — IDs, timestamps, counts, log lines, code, and payloads. Pick a readable default theme.

## Proposed approach

- `apps/ops/src/app/globals.css`: switch `body` to `var(--font-ui)`; introduce a utility (`.mono` class or `[data-mono]` styling on existing value/table-cell classes) applied where alignment or verbatim-data reading matters — timestamps, IDs, queue stats, log entries, `CopyButton` payload text.
- Sweep component modules that currently inherit mono for prose-like text (nav labels, card labels/details, attention items, runbooks, table headers) and confirm they resolve to `--font-ui`; keep mono on genuinely tabular/data cells (queue breakdown stats, log lines, job IDs).
- `apps/ops/src/app/layout.tsx`: change the SSR default theme from `terminal` to the most readable pair (candidate: `grafana` / `grafana-light` — Inter UI + Source Code Pro data). ThemePicker persistence keeps existing user choices.
- Do not add or remove themes in this issue; novelty-theme pruning is a separate decision for the requester.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Computed body/label/heading font on the overview, sources, runs, and logs pages resolves to the theme's `--font-ui` face, while log lines, IDs, and timestamps resolve to `--font` (component or E2E assertion on computed styles for at least one page).
- [ ] The SSR default theme renders sans-serif UI text with no theme-flash regression (existing ThemePicker SSR-correction behavior still passes its tests).
- [ ] All theme pairs still render both fonts correctly (no theme maps prose to a display/pixel face unless the theme's own `--font-ui` is that face — "hacker"/"matrix" remain internally consistent but are no longer the default).
- [ ] Manual QA: side-by-side screenshots of the overview and logs pages (before/after) in the default theme at 375 px and 1280 px confirm prose readability and preserved data alignment.

## Notes

- Related: #755 (contrast pass for muted/status tokens) — same files, different concern; land separately to keep review focused. #442 (closed) introduced the per-theme font system this issue re-balances.
- WCAG 2.1 AA applies (`.claude/core.md`); font-size adjustments that accompany the family switch must not reduce contrast compliance.
- Independent of the triage epic, nav flattening, and #757.

records.title: feat(ops): calm the overview — reserve color and prominence for exceptions
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): calm the overview — reserve color and prominence for exceptions
records.issueBody:
## Context

The ops overview (`apps/ops/src/app/ops/OpsOverviewClient.tsx` + `page.module.css`) renders ~14 metric cards — each with an icon, a severity-colored dot, and a severity-styled border — plus the Attention panel, a per-queue breakdown table, the scrape-run chart, and runbooks, all at the same visual volume. Severity styling is applied even when a card is healthy (`data-severity="good"` still tints icon and dot), so a fully healthy system is as visually busy as a broken one.

The requester's feedback: the console is "so loud" and it is impossible to tell at a glance what actually needs attention. The correct hierarchy for an ops console is the inverse of today's: healthy = quiet, exceptions = prominent.

## Problem / Goal

Rework the overview's visual hierarchy so color, iconography, and prominence are reserved for warning/critical states, and healthy state collapses into compact, low-contrast confirmation.

## Proposed approach

- `page.module.css` / `OpsOverviewClient.tsx`:
  - Healthy (`good`) cards drop the severity dot color, icon tint, and any tinted border — neutral text and border tokens only. `unknown` renders muted, not alarming.
  - Collapse the healthy service cards (api, postgres, valkey, meilisearch, and queues/scraper when clean) into a single compact "All services healthy" row with a timestamp; individual cards render only for degraded services. Keep the per-service detail one click away via `/status`.
  - The Attention panel gets an explicit quiet empty state ("Nothing needs attention") instead of rendering as an always-on alarm-styled card frame.
  - Reduce per-card decoration: one severity signal per card (border OR dot, not both plus icon tint).
- Verify against every ThemePicker theme pair at mobile and desktop widths (severity tokens differ per theme; see #755 for the related contrast pass — coordinate but do not merge scopes).
- Update `OpsOverviewClient.test.tsx` severity-rendering assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With all resources healthy, the overview renders zero warning/critical-colored elements and the service grid is replaced by a single compact healthy-summary row (verified by a component test).
- [ ] A degraded resource renders its card with severity styling while unaffected resources remain in the quiet summary (component test with mixed fixture).
- [ ] The Attention panel renders a quiet empty state when there are no attention items (component test).
- [ ] Each metric card carries at most one severity-colored element in the DOM for its state.
- [ ] Manual QA: screenshots at 375 px and 1280 px for at least the default theme pair confirm the healthy view reads as calm and the degraded view draws the eye only to the degraded items.

## Notes

- Scope is the overview page only; Sources/Runs/Queues tables keep their current styling until the triage epic reworks them.
- WCAG 2.1 AA contrast still applies to the muted healthy styling (`.claude/core.md`); do not fix failures by dropping below AA — coordinate with #755 where token changes are needed.
- The severity model (`OverviewSeverity`, `buildOpsOverview`) is unchanged — this is presentation only, so it stays independent of the triage epic's server-side snapshot move.

records.title: fix(dev): repair devcontainer startup
records.issueTitle: Fix broken and stale devcontainer configuration
records.issueBody:
## Problem

The VS Code devcontainer cannot start because the override assigns the disabled profile to `api`, `web`, and `scraper`, but not `ops`. The active `ops` service still depends on the excluded `api` service, so Docker Compose rejects the merged project with `service "ops" depends on undefined service "api"`.

The devcontainer image manifest copies and named `node_modules` volumes are also stale relative to the current pnpm workspaces, risking failed image installs and Linux dependencies leaking into the host checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The base and devcontainer Compose files merge successfully with `docker compose config`.
- [ ] The devcontainer starts only its development container and required Postgres, Valkey, and Meilisearch dependencies; containerized app services are disabled.
- [ ] Every current app/package workspace needed by `pnpm install` is represented in the dev image manifest layer.
- [ ] Every current app/package workspace keeps container `node_modules` outside the host bind mount.
- [ ] Devcontainer setup installs dependencies and generates the Prisma client successfully.
- [ ] `make dev` can run inside the devcontainer without requiring a Docker CLI or socket.

## Done when

The Compose configuration, dev image build/install, and relevant repository checks pass, with validation commands recorded in the PR.

records.title: chore(infra): stop running E2E smoke and restore-drill on pull_request pushes
records.issueTitle: chore(infra): stop running E2E smoke on every pull_request push
records.issueBody:
## Context
`ci.yml`'s \`e2e\` job (E2E smoke) currently runs on every \`pull_request\` push, every \`merge_group\` run, and every \`push\` to \`main\`. Per \`docs/design/merge-queue.md\`, E2E is deliberately **not** a required merge-queue check — it's signal only, and it also gates the post-merge \`publish\` job on the \`main\` push. Running the full Playwright suite (Docker builds + Chromium install + smoke tests) on every PR commit is slow and adds no blocking value to the PR itself, since it can't stop the merge either way.

## Problem / Goal
Stop the \`e2e\` job from running on \`pull_request\` events in \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\`, while keeping it running on \`merge_group\` (so it still runs before a PR merges) and on \`push\` to \`main\` (so it keeps gating the \`publish\` job exactly as before).

## Proposed approach
- Add a job-level \`if\` condition to the \`e2e\` job in \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\`: \`github.event_name == 'merge_group' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')\`.
- Update \`docs/design/merge-queue.md\`'s "E2E smoke is signal, not a required check" section to describe the new trigger scope instead of "on every PR, merge-group, and main run".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The \`e2e\` job in \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` does not run on a plain \`pull_request\` push (verify via a PR's Actions run showing the job skipped).
- [ ] The \`e2e\` job still runs on \`merge_group\` events and on \`push\` to \`main\`, and \`publish\` still depends on it.
- [ ] \`docs/design/merge-queue.md\` accurately describes the new E2E trigger scope.

## Notes
Related to #715, which originally wired E2E into every trigger including PR pushes.

records.title: feat(ops): flatten navigation — remove single-item group headings and duplicate overview grid
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): flatten navigation — remove single-item group headings and the duplicate overview link grid
records.issueBody:
## Context

The ops left navigation is built from `OPS_NAV_GROUPS` in `apps/ops/src/app/ops/ops-nav.ts`. Six of its eight groups contain exactly one item — "Inventory", "Sources", "Workflows", "Failures", "Schedules", and "Logs" are each a group heading over a single link. The headings double the nav's visual length while adding no hierarchy, and the group names often just restate the child ("Schedules" → "Recurring jobs"). The overview page then duplicates the entire nav a second time as a 9-tile quick-link grid (`getOpsOverviewLinks` rendered at the bottom of `OpsOverviewClient.tsx`).

The requester's feedback: the nav is "really long for no benefit" and the console feels disjointed.

## Problem / Goal

Flatten the primary navigation to a single list of destinations with no single-item group headings, keep genuinely secondary tools tucked under one "Advanced" section, and remove the duplicate quick-link grid from the overview.

## Proposed approach

- `apps/ops/src/app/ops/ops-nav.ts`: collapse the six single-item groups into a flat primary list (Overview, Refresh, Sources, Runs, Schedules, Logs, Source repair, Readiness/Status placement per agreement below). Retain the `advanced` group (Queue diagnostics, AI provider settings, Bull Board) as the only titled section.
- `apps/ops/src/components/OpsNav/*`: render the flat list without group headings; keep the existing mobile tabs / More sheet / rail behavior from E3 (#730) intact — this issue changes the registry shape and desktop/drawer list rendering, not the responsive mechanics.
- `apps/ops/src/app/ops/OpsOverviewClient.tsx` + `page.module.css`: remove the bottom quick-link nav grid (`linkGrid` / `areaLink`); the shell nav is always visible or one tap away, so the duplication serves no purpose.
- Update `ops-nav` unit tests and any OpsShell/OpsNav tests asserting group structure.

Open question to settle in the PR (does not block): whether "Site readiness" and "System status" stay top-level or fold under Overview/Advanced — default to keeping Overview, Readiness, and Status adjacent at the top.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The rendered desktop/drawer navigation contains no group heading whose group has exactly one item; the only titled section remaining is Advanced.
- [ ] All existing routes remain reachable from the nav and direct URLs are unchanged (no route moves in this issue).
- [ ] The overview page no longer renders the quick-link nav grid, and the nav registry's `overviewQuickLink` metadata is removed or repurposed accordingly.
- [ ] Mobile bottom tabs and the More sheet continue to work unchanged (existing E3 tests still pass).
- [ ] Nav registry tests updated to lock the flat structure (a future single-item group addition fails the test with a clear message).

## Notes

- Supersedes the grouping introduced by #338 (closed): grouping by operator intent was right at 10+ prospective pages per group, but the console stabilized at one page per intent, so the headings now only add length.
- Keep `OpsNavGroupId`/metadata changes minimal so the #757 MCP work and the triage epic (which read nav metadata for quick links) are unaffected.

records.title: feat(ops): deep-link failures across runs, sources, and logs via the E6 inspector
records.issueTitle: feat(ops): deep-link failures across runs, sources, queues, and logs via the E6 inspector
records.issueBody:
## Context

E6 (#733) shipped a URL-driven inspector architecture (docked panel / mobile sheet) explicitly designed for cross-page drill-down — and shipped it with **no consumers**. Meanwhile the diagnosis pages barely link to each other:

- A failed run on `/ops/runs` (`RunsClient.tsx`) links nowhere — not to the logs for that run, not to the source that failed. Its only links are "← Operations" and a generic pointer to queue diagnostics.
- `/ops/sources` (`SourcesClient.tsx`) has exactly one deep link (remap job ID → `/ops/logs?search=<jobId>`).
- `/ops/logs` accepts only a bare `?search=` param (`logs/page.tsx`).

The requester's feedback: "there's different pages but I don't know how they interconnect" — diagnosing one failure requires manually copying IDs between pages.

## Problem / Goal

Wire the existing pages together so an operator can go from any visible failure to its evidence and its fix surface in one or two clicks, using the E6 inspector as the drill-down vehicle.

## Proposed approach

- **Runs page** (`apps/ops/src/app/ops/runs/RunsClient.tsx`): each run row opens the E6 inspector with run detail (source, timing, counts, error text) plus links: "Logs for this run" (`/ops/logs` filtered by the run's correlation fields), "Source detail" (`/ops/sources/<id>`), and for failed runs the source's `latestFailedJobId` pipeline context where available (`GET /admin/sources/:id/pipeline` already returns it).
- **Sources pages** (`SourcesClient.tsx`, `sources/[id]`): a source's last error links to the corresponding run row (`/ops/runs` with the run focused via inspector URL state) and to filtered logs.
- **Logs page** (`logs/page.tsx`, `LogsClient.tsx`): accept `service` and time-window params in addition to `search` so inbound deep links can scope precisely (the `/admin/logs` API already supports `service`, `start`, `end`).
- **Queues page**: a queue's failed count links to that queue's failed jobs view (existing `/ops/queues` detail), and failed jobs link to filtered logs by `jobId`.
- Follow the E6 inspector URL contract so drill-down state is shareable/reload-safe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] From a failed run row, the operator reaches (a) logs filtered to that run and (b) the source's detail page without typing or copying any identifier (E2E or component test asserting the generated hrefs/inspector state).
- [ ] From a source's last-error, the operator reaches the corresponding run and its filtered logs in ≤ 2 clicks (test as above).
- [ ] `/ops/logs` honors `service` and time-window query params from inbound links, verified by tests, and `docs/api-routes.md` is untouched (no API changes) or updated if params require API additions.
- [ ] The E6 inspector has at least one shipped consumer (runs drill-down), with its URL state reload-safe (navigating directly to the URL restores the open inspector).
- [ ] Every new link resolves for both success and failure runs (no dead links when optional fields like `latestFailedJobId` are absent — hidden, not broken).

## Notes

- Correlation fields available today: `jobId`, `sourceId`, run IDs, and log labels — the same allow-listed IDs #757's `get_correlation` will use; keep link parameterization consistent with that contract so human and AI drill-down stay symmetric.
- Independent of the triage epic; when the Problems page lands it reuses these same inspector destinations.

records.issueTitle: feat(ui): minimal @wivwav/design-tokens and @wivwav/ui-web foundation package
records.issueBody:
## Context

Depends on #852's spike outcome. Implements the accepted UI foundation per
`docs/design/ui-boundary-and-ops-workspace.md` sections 1 and 4 (decided in
#851).

## Problem / Goal

Create the `@wivwav/design-tokens` and `@wivwav/ui-web` packages as the sole
browser component-vendor boundary for `apps/web` and `apps/ops`, backed by
whichever component system #852's spike accepts.

## Proposed approach

- `@wivwav/design-tokens`: platform-neutral semantic tokens as plain data
  (TS objects/JSON) — color roles, spacing scale, type scale, motion
  durations. No React, DOM, or CSS.
- `@wivwav/ui-web`: provider/theme plus a narrow policy-bearing primitive
  surface (Button, IconButton, Link, Dialog/Drawer, Menu/ContextMenu,
  Tooltip, form controls, status/badge presentation) and any explicitly
  acknowledged vendor re-exports (e.g. a data grid).
- Add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule in `packages/config/eslint.config.js`
  in the same change, so there is never a window where direct vendor imports
  from `apps/web`/`apps/ops` are legal but unenforced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `@wivwav/design-tokens` package exists, exporting platform-neutral semantic tokens as plain data with no React/DOM/CSS dependency.
- [ ] `@wivwav/ui-web` package exists, consuming the component vendor accepted in #852, exporting only the narrow policy-bearing primitive surface (provider/theme, Button, IconButton, Link, Dialog/Drawer, Menu/ContextMenu, Tooltip, form controls, status/badge presentation) plus any explicitly acknowledged vendor re-exports.
- [ ] A Storybook test harness for `@wivwav/ui-web` covers interaction, accessibility (axe), and visual-regression states for each exported primitive.
- [ ] An ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule in `packages/config/eslint.config.js` prevents `apps/web` and `apps/ops` from importing the underlying component vendor or `@emotion/*` directly, landed in this same change.
- [ ] Package build configuration (tsconfig, exports map) follows existing package conventions (see `packages/charts` as reference).
- [ ] No production `apps/web` or `apps/ops` route is migrated in this issue.

## Notes

Depends on #852. Feeds the Ops workspace/panel contract issue and future
incremental `apps/web`/`apps/ops` migration issues.

records.title: chore(infra): rename Dockerfiles into per-service subdirectories for Dependabot
records.issueTitle: chore(infra): rename Dockerfiles so Dependabot docker ecosystem detects them
records.issueBody:
## Context

#602 / PR #689 added a `.github/dependabot.yml` docker ecosystem entry pointed at `/docker`. Dependabot's docker ecosystem only scans files literally named `Dockerfile` in a configured directory — it does not support suffix-style naming. This repo's Dockerfiles use the `<service>.Dockerfile` convention (`docker/api.Dockerfile`, `docker/web.Dockerfile`, `docker/ops.Dockerfile`, `docker/scraper.Dockerfile`, `docker/migrate.Dockerfile`, `docker/dev.Dockerfile`), so the new docker ecosystem entry currently detects zero Dockerfiles and is effectively a no-op placeholder.

`.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is already correctly named (literal `Dockerfile`) but lives outside `/docker` and is not covered by any dependabot entry either.

## Problem / Goal

Restructure the Dockerfiles into per-service subdirectories, each containing a file literally named `Dockerfile`, so Dependabot's docker ecosystem can actually detect and open update PRs for them.

## Proposed approach

1. Move each Dockerfile into its own subdirectory: `docker/api/Dockerfile`, `docker/web/Dockerfile`, `docker/ops/Dockerfile`, `docker/scraper/Dockerfile`, `docker/migrate/Dockerfile`, `docker/dev/Dockerfile`.
2. Update all references (`grep -rn "\.Dockerfile" .github/workflows/ci.yml docker-compose.yml docker-compose.prod.yml`) to the new paths.
3. Add one `.github/dependabot.yml` docker-ecosystem entry per new subdirectory (replacing the single `/docker` placeholder entry from #602), plus one for `.devcontainer` covering `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`.
4. Verify `docker build`/`docker compose build` still succeed locally and that CI's docker build/push steps in `ci.yml` pass with the new paths.

This touches CI build steps and compose files (build/deploy paths), so it should be scoped, reviewed, and tested as its own change rather than bundled into a config-only chore.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All six Dockerfiles under `docker/` are moved into per-service subdirectories, each containing a file literally named `Dockerfile`
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docker-compose.yml`, and `docker-compose.prod.yml` reference the new paths and CI's docker build/push jobs pass
- [ ] `.github/dependabot.yml` has one docker-ecosystem entry per new subdirectory (plus `.devcontainer`) and no longer points at the old flat `/docker` placeholder
- [ ] Manual QA: `docker compose build` succeeds locally for all services after the path changes

## Notes

Related: #602, PR #689 (added the initial `.github/dependabot.yml` with the placeholder `/docker` docker-ecosystem entry and a code comment documenting this exact limitation).

records.title: fix(scraper): repair orphaned listings after authoritative catalog reset
records.issueTitle: fix(search): repair orphaned listings after authoritative catalog reset
records.issueBody:
## Problem

The persisted Meilisearch projection can outlive the authoritative PostgreSQL listing catalog. The incremental checkpoint poller cannot observe hard-deleted rows, so search continues serving orphaned listing IDs; every vehicle card then opens a correct detail 404 rendered as “Listing unavailable.”

Reproduced locally with 0 PostgreSQL listings, 4,814 Meilisearch documents, and a search-returned ID absent from PostgreSQL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When PostgreSQL has no active, publication-eligible listings but the live search index still contains documents, the single-owner indexer repairs the projection automatically.
- [ ] Repair uses the existing versioned-index build and atomic swap; the live index is not cleared in place.
- [ ] A current, publication-eligible listing returned from search remains resolvable by the detail endpoint.
- [ ] Removed, ineligible, or unknown listings still return 404.
- [ ] Automated regression coverage exercises orphan repair, an already-empty catalog, successful detail, and genuine not-found behavior.
- [ ] Relevant scraper/API checks pass.

records.title: docs(design): consolidate converged /admin-elimination decision record for #843
records.issueTitle: discussion(security): eliminate /admin URLs and ratify the private ops control plane
records.issueBody:
## Purpose

Ratify and track a stricter privileged-control boundary for WivWav before implementation. The owner requirement is explicit: **no WivWav-owned runtime URL may use the `/admin` namespace**.

This is an architecture/decision issue first. Claude must independently review the evidence and candidate design, a human owner must resolve the decisions, and only then should implementation child issues be finalized and marked ready.

## Goals

1. Eliminate `/admin` from WivWav-owned API routes, browser/BFF requests, Bull Board links/assets, tests, current documentation, and deployment examples.
2. Keep intentionally public product capabilities distinct from privileged operator capabilities.
3. Make privileged capabilities unreachable through public web ingress and fail closed at the application boundary as defense in depth.
4. Keep the human operator UI under `/ops/*`, in its separate container, with the option to stop it by default and start it securely on demand.
5. Preserve the existing session-authenticated ops BFF and server-held credential model established by #450.
6. Coordinate this change with the open AI Diagnostic Gateway work (#773, #775, #778, #780).

## Current evidence

- `apps/api/src/app.ts` mounts queue controls, schedules, source controls, config, logs, AI operations, listing triage, and Bull Board under `/admin/*`. The common `adminAuthPlugin` is fail-closed in production, so authorization exists, but the namespace and edge exposure policy do not meet the new requirement.
- `apps/ops` protects operator pages with a signed session and proxies server-side through its BFF, but browser-side BFF URLs still contain paths such as `/api/bff/admin/*`; Bull Board is exposed on the ops origin at `/admin/board/*`.
- Bull Board currently relies on identical upstream and proxy base paths because its generated asset/API URLs use the configured base path. Its migration needs a tested proxy/base-path design, not a string-only rename.
- `apps/web/src/lib/resolve-ollama-config.ts` performs a server-to-server decrypted-config lookup through `/admin/config/:key/decrypt`. This is service-to-service configuration access, not a human operator action, and may deserve its own internal scope.
- `docker-compose.prod.yml` publishes API port 3001 and ops port 3002 on the host. Whether they are Internet-reachable depends on infrastructure not defined in the repository; there is no checked-in reverse-proxy/path-allowlist contract.
- `/v1/*` is an intentional public product/API-key surface and should not be conflated with privileged controls.
- Diagnostic issues #773/#775/#778/#780 currently refer to `/admin/*` for asymmetric authorization tests or read-only wrappers and must be reconciled before implementation.

## Candidate route and trust model

This is a proposal for Claude/human review, not yet a ratified contract.

| Caller / capability | Candidate URL | Exposure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public website | `/*` | Public |
| Public product API | `/v1/*` | Intentionally public; API-key/trusted-origin policy, validation, and rate limits remain |
| Operator UI | `/ops/*` | Ops origin only; human session required |
| Ops browser-to-BFF calls | `/ops/api/*` | Same ops origin; human session + CSRF checks |
| Privileged operator API | `/internal/ops/*` | Private service network only; server credential; fail closed |
| Service config retrieval | `/internal/config/*` or another purpose-specific internal scope | Private service network only; least-privilege decision required |
| Bull Board | `/ops/queues/board/*` on ops origin, mapped to a private upstream | Human session required; generated asset/API paths must remain functional |
| AI diagnostics | `/diagnostics/*` or a revised internal/remote diagnostic scope | Separate read-only credential and exposure policy owned by milestone 21 |

The old `/admin/*` paths should not remain as redirects or compatibility aliases in the completed state. They should be unregistered and return 404. Because aliases are undesirable, rollout must coordinate API, ops, web server-side callers, tests, and documentation without leaving `main` in a broken intermediate state.

## Decisions requested

### D1 - Namespace ownership

Confirm or revise the candidate namespaces. In particular, decide whether server-to-server secret/config retrieval belongs under `/internal/ops` or a narrower `/internal/config` capability with a distinct authorization scope.

### D2 - Public versus private API

Confirm that `/v1/*` remains an intentionally public, untrusted product interface while privileged control routes are reachable only on the private service network. Document explicit exceptions such as health, metrics, telemetry, webhooks, OpenAPI, and diagnostics.

### D3 - Bull Board proxy contract

Choose and prove a base-path/proxy mapping that serves the board only at `/ops/queues/board/*` on the authenticated ops origin while its API upstream remains private. Tests must cover HTML, generated static assets, API calls, nested paths, unauthenticated navigation, and unauthenticated subresource requests.

### D4 - Deployment and ingress enforcement

Define executable production exposure rules: which services bind host ports, which reverse proxy joins the private network, exact allowed public paths/hosts, health-check reachability, and how direct access to privileged routes is denied. Application bearer auth remains defense in depth, not the sole edge control.

### D5 - Migration and rollback

Decide the coordinated release sequence with no permanent `/admin` alias. Include rollback behavior and account for the web server's internal config call, the ops BFF, Bull Board, and diagnostic-gateway branches.

### D6 - On-demand ops lifecycle

Define the hosting-specific design for ops being stopped by default, authenticated startup outside the stopped container, readiness/cold-start behavior, optional idle shutdown, auditability, and a manual fallback. An unauthenticated public "wake ops" endpoint is forbidden.

## Claude review request

Claude should inspect the cited files and comment with **AGREE**, **AGREE WITH CHANGES**, or **DISAGREE**, followed by evidence and concrete revisions.

Please address:

1. Is `/internal/ops/*` the correct private Fastify namespace, and should decrypted config retrieval use a narrower separate scope?
2. Is `/ops/api/*` an appropriate same-origin BFF path, or is another ops-only namespace cleaner?
3. What Bull Board base-path/proxy arrangement avoids URL rewriting bugs while ensuring no `/admin` path exists?
4. Should the production API share one listener for public and internal routes behind an ingress allowlist, use separate listeners, or split deployment units? Which is proportional for WivWav?
5. Are no compatibility aliases and a coordinated deployment reasonable, or is a tightly bounded transition safer?
6. What automated checks best prove privileged routes are not reachable through public ingress?
7. How should #773/#775/#778/#780 change without weakening the diagnostic gateway's asymmetric credential model?
8. Which parts are over-engineering for the current deployment?

## Candidate implementation tracks after ratification

1. **Namespace migration:** change the API mount and auth terminology; migrate ops BFF clients, the web server config caller, Bull Board, tests, and canonical route docs as one coherent cross-app contract.
2. **Exposure enforcement:** harden Compose/production ingress, document explicit route allowlists and service bindings, and add black-box tests proving privileged paths are unreachable publicly.
3. **Regression guard:** add a targeted repository/runtime assertion preventing reintroduction of WivWav-owned `/admin` URLs while permitting immutable historical or third-party references where necessary.
4. **On-demand ops:** implement the provider-specific stopped-by-default/start-on-request/idle-stop workflow only after the production hosting control plane is selected.

The final issue graph may combine tracks 2 and 3. Do not create implementation tickets mechanically until D1-D6 are ratified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Claude posts an evidence-backed review answering all eight review questions.
- [ ] A human owner records D1-D6 as accepted, revised, or rejected.
- [ ] The ratified route matrix identifies every public, ops-session, internal-service, diagnostic, webhook, health, metrics, telemetry, and documentation surface.
- [ ] The ratified design guarantees no WivWav-owned runtime URL uses `/admin`; the retired paths return 404 with no redirect or compatibility alias in the completed state.
- [ ] The design specifies Bull Board base-path behavior and tests for generated assets/API URLs.
- [ ] The design specifies production network/ingress enforcement and black-box negative tests for privileged-route reachability.
- [ ] The design specifies a coordinated migration, rollback, and smoke-check sequence.
- [ ] #773, #775, #778, and #780 receive explicit compatible dispositions before any is implemented.
- [ ] Child issues are created with concrete acceptance criteria, dependencies, rollout/rollback notes, and validation evidence; only dependency-free work receives `status:ready`.
- [ ] The milestone tracking list records canonical execution order and closes last.

## Non-goals

- Removing or hiding the intentionally public `/v1/*` product API solely because it is an API.
- Treating a nonstandard URL as a security control.
- Removing fail-closed application authorization after network isolation is added.
- Splitting the repository or introducing unrelated microservices.
- Implementing an unauthenticated public endpoint that starts the ops service.
- Editing historical GitHub issue text or third-party URL references that are not WivWav-owned runtime routes.

## Done when

Claude and the human owner have ratified the boundary, the dependent issue graph is consistent, all implementation tracks are complete with evidence, no WivWav-owned `/admin` URL remains, public-ingress tests reject privileged access, and this tracking issue closes last.

records.title: feat(misc): establish a shared web UI boundary and dynamic Ops workspace foundation
records.issueTitle: design(ui): establish a shared web UI boundary and dynamic Ops workspace foundation
records.issueBody:
## Context

The Ops console is currently organized primarily as routes containing lists and one-off detail surfaces. Operational concepts are related across sources, scraper runs, jobs, logs, vehicles, search data, and infrastructure telemetry, but those relationships are difficult to follow in the UI.

The desired direction is a responsive workspace that can open contextual detail panels, span panels across grid columns, resize or maximize a panel, preserve deep links, and expose the same entity actions through visible buttons, overflow menus, keyboard-accessible context menus, and eventually a command surface. Panels should support live status, configuration, logs, errors, metrics, and related entities without forcing the operator to manually copy identifiers between pages.

At the same time, WivWav should minimize application-owned generic UI code. `apps/ops` currently owns substantial CSS Module, theme, navigation, inspector, focus-management, and responsive-shell behavior. `apps/web` already has a separate styling/component stack. A future consumer mobile app may use React Native, so browser/DOM-specific components should not be presented as platform-neutral UI.

This is an architecture and decomposition issue. It does not authorize implementation directly.

## Problem / Goal

Agree on a maintainable UI boundary and migration plan that:

- gives Web and Ops one tested browser-component dependency surface;
- delegates generic accessibility and interaction behavior to maintained dependencies;
- keeps WivWav-specific domain components and workflows under WivWav control;
- enables the dynamic Ops workspace without making every screen a custom layout system;
- keeps platform-neutral types, domain logic, API access, and design semantics reusable by a future native app; and
- satisfies WivWav's runtime-license policy with an exact-version and transitive-dependency review.

## Proposed starting point for discussion

This is a proposal, not a settled decision:

```text
                         @wivwav/types
                  platform-neutral domain logic
                API client and semantic design tokens
                         /               \
              @wivwav/ui-web       @wivwav/ui-native (future)
                 /       \                  |
            apps/web   apps/ops       React Native app
```

- Create `@wivwav/ui-web` as the only browser UI dependency surface used by Web and Ops.
- Back it with a maintained component system, with MUI Core and MUI X Community as the current leading candidate rather than a decision already made.
- Keep the dependency implementation private to `@wivwav/ui-web`; prohibit direct vendor-component imports from the apps with lint rules.
- Expose a small WivWav API for shared primitives and conventions. Avoid thin wrappers that merely duplicate every vendor prop.
- Keep product composites local until genuinely shared: for example, `OpsPanel`, `RunTimeline`, and `LogViewer` stay Ops-owned; `ListingCard` stays Web-owned.
- Use Storybook as the isolated catalog, interaction-test surface, accessibility-test surface, and visual-regression surface for WivWav-owned web components. Do not duplicate vendor-library stories.
- Begin with one restrained semantic visual system and automatic light/dark behavior. A glass treatment and the existing large set of Ops theme variants are not architectural requirements.
- Use ordinary CSS Grid for spanning dashboard panels and add a focused split/resizing dependency only where operator-controlled resizing is needed. Defer arbitrary drag-and-drop dashboard construction.
- Treat `@wivwav/ui-web` and the current Recharts/Radix-backed `@wivwav/charts` as browser-specific. A future `@wivwav/ui-native` would translate shared semantic tokens into native components rather than attempting to render MUI on React Native.

## Decisions required before implementation

1. **Package boundary:** Is `@wivwav/ui-web` the correct public boundary, and which code belongs in shared primitives versus app-local composites?
2. **Component dependency:** Does MUI Core + MUI X Community produce less owned code and acceptable bundle/runtime behavior for both `apps/web` and `apps/ops`, or should another candidate be spiked?
3. **Vendor leakage:** Which component APIs should WivWav normalize, which may be direct re-exports, and how do we avoid either lock-in leakage or an expensive wrapper framework?
4. **Tokens and theming:** Should semantic design tokens be a separate platform-neutral package immediately? How are the current Ops variants and Web seasonal themes migrated or retired without a big-bang rewrite?
5. **Ops workspace model:** Define panel identity, entity context, URL/deep-link state, layout presets, scroll ownership, responsive behavior, resize, maximize/restore, focus handling, and action placement.
6. **Testing:** Define the boundary among package unit tests, Storybook interaction/accessibility/visual tests, app integration tests, and end-to-end workflow tests.
7. **Mobile seam:** Identify what is truly portable—types, validation, formatters, domain logic, API client, query semantics, and design tokens—while keeping DOM, routing, authentication storage, charts, and native navigation platform-specific.
8. **Licensing:** Audit exact pinned versions and transitive runtime licenses. Reconcile the core allowlist (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, PostgreSQL License) with existing ISC-licensed Lucide usage, and specify notice/SBOM/CI enforcement.
9. **Migration:** Choose an incremental adoption order that avoids rewriting both apps at once and preserves existing routes, accessibility, and operational workflows.

## Coordination with existing work

- #761 already proposes URL-driven cross-page drill-down through the E6 inspector. Decide whether that inspector becomes the first workspace panel implementation, is adapted, or is superseded.
- #758's unified Problems surface should consume the same entity relationships, evidence links, and panel conventions.
- #760 and #762 contain useful visual-hierarchy and typography requirements that should survive any component-library change.
- #755 audits a theme system that may be simplified. Decide whether its remaining work still applies, is narrowed to retained themes, or is superseded.
- The shared package must follow `docs/BRAND.md`, WCAG 2.1 AA, the API-first boundary, and mobile-first consumer workflows.

## Non-goals

- Building the native application now.
- Recreating a foundational component system from scratch.
- Requiring a glass appearance.
- Providing a fully arbitrary draggable dashboard in the first iteration.
- Performing a big-bang rewrite of either application.
- Moving Ops-only or Web-only composites into a shared package without demonstrated reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Codex and Claude record signed architecture-review comments on this issue, including explicit agreements, disagreements, risks, and a recommended first slice.
- [ ] The discussion reaches or escalates a decision for each of the nine decision areas above; unresolved product choices are clearly assigned to the maintainer rather than silently assumed.
- [ ] A dependency/license matrix records exact candidate packages, versions, direct and transitive runtime licenses, commercial-feature boundaries, notice obligations, and compatibility with `.claude/core.md`.
- [ ] A package dependency diagram and import rules distinguish shared platform-neutral code, `@wivwav/ui-web`, app-local composites, and a future native implementation.
- [ ] The Ops workspace contract covers panel identity, entity relationships, URL state, layout/span/resize/maximize behavior, accessibility, and narrow-screen behavior.
- [ ] The test strategy assigns unit, Storybook interaction/accessibility/visual, integration, and end-to-end coverage without duplicating vendor tests.
- [ ] Existing issues #755, #758, #760, #761, and #762 are explicitly retained, revised, blocked, or superseded.
- [ ] Implementation is decomposed into small child issues with acceptance criteria and an incremental migration order; this decision issue is not implemented directly.

## Requested reviewer format

Each participant should sign their own issue comment and separate:

1. Agreements
2. Disagreements or corrections
3. Risks and missing decisions
4. Recommended first implementation slice

— Codex (OpenAI)

records.title: fix(scraper): stop BLVD pagination gracefully on any page 2+ nav error
records.issueTitle: bug(scraper): BLVD source run aborts entire scrape and discards all listings on transient page-2+ navigation error
records.issueBody:
## Context
A BLVD source run failed with \`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'id')\` recorded as the run's error message, with the run failing after several minutes (well into pagination).

Investigation traced the root cause to \`apps/scraper/src/sources/blvd.ts\`'s pagination loop (\`BlvdAdapter.scrape\`). No unguarded \`.id\` access exists anywhere in the ingest/claims pipeline (\`listing-ingest.ts\`, \`card-claims.ts\`, \`claims-repository.ts\`, \`prisma-repositories.ts\` were all audited — every nullable Prisma lookup is properly guarded).

Instead, the bug is in the page.goto() catch block for \`pageNum > 1\`:

\`\`\`ts
} catch (err) {
  if (pageNum > 1 && isNavigationTimeout(err)) {
    // ...graceful stop, keep already-scraped listings
    break
  }
  throw err
}
\`\`\`

Only navigation *timeouts* are treated as recoverable past page 1. Any other transient error during a later page's navigation — e.g. the well-known \`puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth\` evasion-script race against page teardown/navigation (which throws exactly \`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'id')\`), or \`net::ERR_ABORTED\`-style errors — rethrows and propagates out of \`adapter.scrape()\`, is caught by \`ScraperEngine.runSource()\`'s outer catch, and aborts the **entire run**, discarding every listing already collected across however many prior pages.

BLVD is uniquely exposed among WivWav's sources because it reuses a single \`page\` object across many sequential \`page.goto()\` calls in an unbounded pagination loop, unlike sources with a small fixed page count.

## Problem / Goal
Any transient navigation error encountered while paginating past page 1 should stop pagination gracefully (preserving already-scraped listings for this run), not abort the whole source run and discard all prior work — mirroring how navigation timeouts already behave.

## Proposed approach
In \`apps/scraper/src/sources/blvd.ts\`, broaden the \`pageNum > 1\` catch branch in \`BlvdAdapter.scrape()\` to treat any error (not just \`isNavigationTimeout\`) as a signal to stop pagination gracefully, reporting the actual error message and a \`page_error\` reason code (vs. the existing \`page_timeout\` reason) for the non-timeout case. Page 1 remains strict (still uses \`withNavigationRetry\`, which only retries timeouts), since a page 1 failure means zero listings for that path regardless.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A non-timeout error thrown from \`page.goto()\` on page 2+ of BLVD pagination stops pagination and returns the listings already scraped, instead of throwing out of \`adapter.scrape()\`.
- [ ] A non-timeout error on page 2+ is reported via \`report()\` with \`reason: 'page_error'\` (timeouts keep \`reason: 'page_timeout'\`), including the underlying error message in the log text.
- [ ] Page 1 navigation failures (any error type) still propagate and fail the run, unchanged from current behavior.
- [ ] Existing BLVD unit/gold test suites (\`blvd.test.ts\`, \`blvd.gold.test.ts\`) pass unmodified in behavior for previously-covered cases, plus new coverage for the page 2+ non-timeout-error graceful-stop path.

## Notes
Investigated via direct code audit of the BLVD adapter, \`ScraperEngine.runSource()\`, \`listing-ingest.ts\`, \`card-claims.ts\`, and \`claims-repository.ts\` — confirmed no unguarded \`.id\` dereference exists in application code. Related prior BLVD pagination-robustness fix: #484 (ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES at page 8, unrelated failure mode, already fixed).

Parent epic: #129. Depends on: #798. No public UI should consume this until #798/#797 have real calibration data — this issue only builds the read model and its threshold enforcement.

records.title: feat(queue): semantic image-analysis queue and scoped backfill trigger
records.issueTitle: feat(queue): semantic image-analysis queue and scoped backfill trigger
records.issueBody:
## Context

#797 adds the ability to run one semantic classification (ramp-photo evidence) against a single listing image. To apply this across the existing catalog and to new listings as they're scraped, we need a queue/worker and a bounded, observable backfill trigger — following the same operational pattern as #503's integrity backfill.

## Problem / Goal

Add a queue that enqueues integrity-eligible listing images (per #503's eligibility rules — excluding placeholders/cross-vehicle anomalies) that are missing semantic analysis or stale relative to the current semantic-analysis version (from #796/#797), and processes them idempotently and with rate limiting.

## Proposed approach

- New queue (e.g. `image-semantic-analyze`) with a worker that calls the #797 classification logic per image.
- Enqueue criteria: image passes #503 integrity eligibility AND (no semantic attempt record exists OR existing record's semantic version is stale).
- Rate-limited processing to bound cost/API load.
- Admin/report trigger (script or admin route) that reports counts (eligible, already analyzed, to-be-enqueued) and estimated cost/failure reasons before enqueuing broadly — mirrors #506's containment-before-broad-application posture.
- Handle: missing photos, changed bytes at a stable URL, model errors, malformed JSON, retry exhaustion, rate-limit backoff, and safe reruns.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Running the admin/report trigger against seeded data reports the correct count of eligible-but-unanalyzed images without enqueuing anything (dry-run/report mode).
- [ ] Enqueuing processes only integrity-eligible images missing or stale on semantic version; already-current images are skipped.
- [ ] A worker run against a mix of valid and error-inducing images completes without crashing the queue, and failures are recorded per #797's attempt-record schema rather than silently dropped.
- [ ] Tests cover: eligibility filtering, staleness detection, and idempotent re-enqueue (no duplicate processing of already-current images).

## Notes
Parent epic: #129. Depends on: #797 (classification logic must exist first). Related: #503 (integrity eligibility rules, rate-limit/backfill pattern precedent).
