records.title: chore(search): align mileage bucket width with the 12k/year benchmark
records.issueTitle: chore(search): align mileage histogram bucket width with the 12k/year mileage benchmark
records.issueBody:
## Context
The Discover page's mileage histogram/range control buckets listings by mileage using `mileageBucket()` in `packages/search/src/index.ts`, which defaults `bucketSize` to 25,000 miles. That width was never chosen deliberately — it was introduced with no comment or rationale alongside `priceBucket()` in commit `78dd509` (#139), and simply carried a similar shape (`Math.floor(x / size) * size`).

25,000 miles has no relationship to how buyers actually think about vehicle mileage. The used-auto industry runs on a ~12,000-mile-per-year benchmark (the default mileage allowance in most lease agreements, and the yardstick dealer/CARFAX-style reports use to flag a vehicle as high- or low-mileage for its age). A 12,000-mile bucket width would make each bar roughly correspond to "one year of typical driving," which is a much more legible unit for a buyer scanning the distribution than an arbitrary 25k-mile band.

## Problem / Goal
Change the mileage histogram's bucket width from 25,000 to 12,000 miles so the buckets align with the standard annual-mileage benchmark, and make sure the change propagates correctly through the whole pipeline: the Meilisearch document field (`mileageBucket`), the API facets response (`apps/api/src/services/listing-facets.ts`), and the web histogram component (`apps/web/src/components/MileageHistogram.tsx`).

`mileageBucket` is computed and stored on the Meilisearch document at index time, not derived per-query, so existing indexed listings will carry stale 25k-wide bucket values until they're re-synced. The change needs to account for getting the existing index onto the new bucket width (via the existing full reconciliation path in `apps/scraper/src/jobs/search-reconciliation.ts`, a scheduled or manually triggered reindex, or equivalent), not just the code default.

## Proposed approach
- `packages/search/src/index.ts`: change `mileageBucket(mileage, bucketSize = 25000)` to `bucketSize = 12000`.
- `apps/web/src/components/MileageHistogram.tsx`: `BUCKET_SIZE_MILES` is currently `10000` and is only used as a `parseBucket()` fallback when a bucket string has no explicit `hi` value (the API always sends `lo-hi`, so this fallback is presently dead in practice) — update it to `12000` for consistency, or confirm and document that it's unreachable.
- Confirm whether the reconciliation/reindex job needs to be run once against staging/production after deploy, and record that as a deployment step rather than assuming the nightly job alone is sufficient before the next scheduled run.
- Update any fixture/test expectations that hard-code the old 25,000-mile bucket math (e.g. `e2e/support/facets-catalog.ts` / `e2e/tests/discover-facets.spec.ts` if their fixture mileages were chosen to land on 25k boundaries — recompute against 12k boundaries and adjust `wavFeatures`/mileage docs or expected counts as needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `mileageBucket()` in `packages/search/src/index.ts` defaults to a 12,000-mile bucket width, verified by a unit test asserting bucket boundaries for representative mileages (e.g. 0, 11999, 12000, 23999, 24000).
- [ ] The web mileage histogram (`apps/web/src/components/MileageHistogram.tsx`) renders bars matching the new 12,000-mile bucket width against a fixture-backed facets response, with no leftover reference to the old 25,000/10,000-mile widths.
- [ ] Any e2e/integration fixtures whose expected mileage-bucket counts depend on the old 25,000-mile width are recomputed and pass against the 12,000-mile width.
- [ ] The PR documents how the existing Meilisearch index gets re-synced onto the new bucket width post-deploy (reconciliation job trigger, manual reindex command, or equivalent), so production facet data doesn't serve stale 25k-wide buckets indefinitely.
- [ ] Manual QA: load Discover with a seeded/fixture catalog spanning a range of mileages and confirm the mileage histogram bars and range-slider ticks visually correspond to ~12k-mile increments.

## Notes
Related: #641 (fixture-backed Discover facets browser coverage, which surfaced the mileage-bucket math while reviewing a PR) and #139 (original introduction of `mileageBucket()`/`priceBucket()`, no rationale recorded for either bucket width).

records.title: fix(scraper,ops): cold-start drift false positives, sync UI crash, invisible tooltips
records.issueTitle: bug(scraper): source-drift cold-start false positives, Meilisearch sync UI crash, and invisible ops tooltips
records.issueBody:
## Context
While investigating why BLVD.com, MobilityWorks, and Superior Van & Mobility source scrapes were all paused with "Source quality drifted abruptly" messages, plus two ops UI reports (a crash when triggering Meilisearch sync, and invisible tooltip text on the Advanced Queue Diagnostics page), found three distinct, previously-unreported bugs.

### 1. Source-drift cold-start false positives
Observed: `sources` rows for BLVD.com, MobilityWorks, and Superior Van & Mobility were all created within the same second (2026-07-09 23:27:39) and paused on their very first scrape with messages like:
- `Source quality drifted abruptly — missing rate 21.4% vs baseline 0.0% (threshold 15 pts)`
- `Source quality drifted abruptly — missing rate 50.0% vs baseline 0.0% (threshold 15 pts)`
- `Source quality drifted abruptly — missing rate 62.7% vs baseline 12.5% (threshold 15 pts)`

Root cause: `getDriftBaseline()` in `apps/scraper/src/infrastructure/prisma-repositories.ts` defaulted a never-recorded (`null`) baseline to `0`. Every source's first-ever scrape was therefore compared against an implicit 0% baseline in `detectSourceDrift()` (`apps/scraper/src/engine/listing-validator.ts`), so any nonzero missing/error rate — normal for a real site — exceeded the 15-point threshold and the source was immediately (and permanently, since a paused source never scrapes again) paused.

### 2. Meilisearch sync UI crash
Observed: clicking "Sync" on the ops Advanced Queue Diagnostics page throws `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.data.synced.toLocaleString')`.

Root cause: `POST /admin/sync` (`apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts`) returns `{ data: { enqueued, jobId } }` (it enqueues an async BullMQ job), but `apps/ops/src/app/ops/queues/QueuesClient.tsx` assumed a synchronous `{ data: { synced: number } }` response and called `.toLocaleString()` on the nonexistent `synced` field.

### 3. Invisible ops tooltips
Observed: info-icon tooltips on the Advanced Queue Diagnostics page render as blank/black boxes with no visible text in several themes.

Root cause: `.tip::after` in `apps/ops/src/app/ops/ops.module.css` pairs `background: var(--clr-header-bg)` with `color: var(--clr-text)` instead of `var(--clr-header-text)` — the variable every other component (e.g. `OpsHeader.module.css`) pairs with `--clr-header-bg`. In themes such as `dracula-light`, `tokyo-light`, `catppuccin-light`, and `classic`, `--clr-header-bg` and `--clr-text` are both dark, producing unreadable dark-on-dark tooltip text.

## Problem / Goal
Fix all three defects so that:
- New or freshly-reset sources are never falsely paused for "abrupt drift" on their first scrape.
- The ops sync button reflects the real (async, job-enqueuing) API contract without crashing.
- Diagnostics-page tooltips are legible in every theme.

## Proposed approach
1. `apps/scraper/src/engine/repositories.ts` / `prisma-repositories.ts`: change `getDriftBaseline()` to return `SourceDriftBaseline | null` (null when the source has no recorded baseline yet) instead of defaulting to zeros.
2. `apps/scraper/src/engine/listing-validator.ts`: `detectSourceDrift()` accepts `baseline: SourceDriftBaseline | null`; when `null`, never flags drift and seeds `nextBaseline` from the current observation.
3. `apps/scraper/src/jobs/listing-quality-audit.ts`: pass `null` instead of a synthetic zero baseline into `detectSourceDrift()`, for the same reason.
4. `apps/ops/src/app/ops/queues/QueuesClient.tsx`: update `triggerSync()` to parse `{ data: { enqueued, jobId } }` and show a "Sync queued (job {jobId})" message instead of a listing count that's never returned.
5. `apps/ops/src/app/ops/ops.module.css`: change `.tip::after`'s `color` from `var(--clr-text)` to `var(--clr-header-text)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `detectSourceDrift(null, observation)` returns `drifted: false` and seeds `nextBaseline` from the observation (unit test).
- [ ] A source with no prior baseline that has a high missing/error rate on its first scrape is not paused (unit/integration test on `scraper-engine`).
- [ ] Triggering sync on the ops Advanced Queue Diagnostics page shows a "queued" confirmation instead of throwing a TypeError, matching the actual `/admin/sync` response shape.
- [ ] Manual QA: tooltips on the ops Advanced Queue Diagnostics page show legible text in at least one light theme (e.g. `classic` or `dracula-light`) and one dark theme.

## Notes
BLVD.com, MobilityWorks, and Superior Van & Mobility remain paused in the current environment from before this fix; they were left as-is pending manual re-activation since flipping source status/baselines is a live-data change outside the scope of a code fix.

records.title: test(search): add a fixture-to-facets pipeline contract suite
records.issueTitle: test(search): add a fixture-to-facets pipeline contract suite
records.issueBody:
## Problem

Facet tests currently mock Meilisearch distributions, scraper tests mock persistence/search boundaries, and Meilisearch-sync tests mock both PostgreSQL and Meilisearch. Each layer can pass while the combined pipeline loses fields, leaves listings pending, indexes duplicates, or serves incorrect counts.

The recent catalog audit found all of those failure modes:

- detail-extracted accessibility values overwritten by card recrawls (#633)
- resolution jobs never consumed (#634)
- source-specific detail jobs not scheduled (#635)
- duplicate vehicle documents emitted by full search rebuilds (#636)
- partial detail failures hidden as completed jobs (#637)

## Goal

Add a hermetic fixture-to-facets integration suite using isolated real PostgreSQL and Meilisearch services. Exercise the production data transformations synchronously and assert exact, hand-authored facet distributions and filtering behavior.

## Controlled catalog

Use a small checked-in catalog manifest backed by the offline source fixtures. It must include:

- BLVD and MobilityWorks listings
- new/used and dealer/private values
- rear/side/unknown entry types
- in-floor/fold-out/unknown ramps
- multiple WAV features
- conversion-brand aliases
- canonical make/model/color cases
- price and mileage bucket boundaries
- multiple states and trims
- duplicate rows sharing one verified vehicle identity
- pending, quarantined, gone, and eligible rows
- optional-field absence

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The suite starts from isolated, disposable PostgreSQL and Meilisearch state and never mutates a developer database/index.
- [ ] Fixture-derived card observations are persisted through the production repository path.
- [ ] Fixture-derived detail observations are applied through the production detail-update path.
- [ ] Publication resolution, representative selection/deduplication, search-document canonicalization, and full Meilisearch sync use production code.
- [ ] Meilisearch tasks are awaited before assertions.
- [ ] `GET /v1/listings/facets` exactly matches a hand-authored expected manifest for total, make, model, trim, year, price, mileage, state, condition, conversion type, color, ramp type, seller type, conversion brand, and WAV features.
- [ ] Total equals eligible unique vehicle groups, not raw listing rows.
- [ ] Pending, quarantined, and gone listings are absent from search and facets.
- [ ] A duplicate vehicle group contributes exactly one deterministic representative.
- [ ] For every supported facet value, the corresponding `GET /v1/listings` filter returns the expected total.
- [ ] Combined-filter and range-filter cases are covered.
- [ ] Disjunctive-faceting requests used by the web client are covered.
- [ ] A second recrawl phase verifies updates, detail-field preservation, deletion/exclusion, cache behavior, and reindexing.
- [ ] Multi-valued WAV feature counts are tested without applying invalid exclusive-facet sum invariants.
- [ ] Failures identify the pipeline checkpoint that diverged: parsed observation, database row, publication decision, search document, facet API, or filtered listing API.
- [ ] The suite has a documented local command and a bounded CI runtime target.

## Dependencies

- #639
- #633
- #634
- #636

#635 and #637 should have their own orchestration tests; the core facet contract invokes processors synchronously rather than waiting on cron/BullMQ timing.

## Scope boundary

Do not use live source websites for exact-count assertions. Do not derive the expected facet manifest using the same production aggregation code being tested.

records.title: feat(scraper): singleton scheduler, source registry, and queue policies
records.issueTitle: feat(scraper): singleton scheduler, declarative source registry, and per-queue policies
records.issueBody:
## Context

Ratified decision D5 in #666 (beta scope). The scraper composition root (`apps/scraper/src/index.ts`, 588 lines) registers every source, worker, queue, and repeatable schedule in one process; every replica runs everything and participates in schedule registration (the #631/#635 collision class). `SCRAPER_CONCURRENCY` is documented in `.env.example` but read nowhere. Completed/failed job retention is undefined. Source metadata, adapter registration, pipeline capabilities, and schedule definitions are maintained in multiple places.

## Problem / Goal

1. A singleton scheduler role: schedule registration happens exactly once regardless of replica count.
2. One declarative source registry owning adapter, metadata, schedules, and pipeline capabilities per source.
3. Per-queue concurrency, retry/idempotency, timeout, and completed/failed retention policies wired through `packages/queue`.

Deferred by decision: splitting browser/data/indexer into separate processes — do not implement until workload evidence requires it.

## Proposed approach

Introduce a runtime-mode flag (scheduler vs worker) in the bootstrap; extract a `sources/registry.ts` consumed by bootstrap, ops schedule views, and pipeline code; move per-queue policy into queue definitions in `packages/queue`; wire `SCRAPER_CONCURRENCY` or replace it with per-queue settings and update `.env.example` accordingly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Running N scraper replicas registers each repeatable schedule exactly once (regression test covering the #631/#635 collision class)
- [ ] Adding a new source requires touching only the registry plus its adapter module; bootstrap, schedules, and ops views derive from the registry
- [ ] Per-queue concurrency and completed/failed retention are configured and observable; no documented-but-unread env vars remain

## Notes

From #666 (D5, ratified 2026-07-05). Coordinate with #631/#635, which are authorized to land first as immediate fixes; this issue then owns the structural prevention. Likely split before implementation.

records.title: feat(observability): reconcile every facet between PostgreSQL and Meilisearch
records.issueTitle: feat(observability): reconcile every facet between PostgreSQL and Meilisearch
records.issueBody:
## Problem

Fixture tests cannot detect live source drift, stalled enrichment, stale publication decisions, cache/index divergence, or field coverage collapsing after deployment.

The existing listing-quality audit compares raw eligible listing rows with Meilisearch document count. Search is intended to contain one representative per verified vehicle group, so that comparison can report the wrong expected count. It also does not compare individual facet distributions or coverage by source.

Relevant paths:

- `apps/scraper/src/jobs/listing-quality-audit.ts`
- `docs/ops/runbook-listing-quality-audit.md`
- `apps/api/src/services/listing-facets.ts`
- `packages/search/src/index.ts`

## Goal

Extend operational auditing to reconcile the eligible representative catalog with Meilisearch and monitor field/facet coverage without treating legitimately optional fields as required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Expected search-document total uses eligible unique vehicle groups and the same deterministic representative-selection policy as indexing.
- [ ] The audit detects duplicate non-null `vehicleId` values in Meilisearch.
- [ ] The audit compares PostgreSQL-derived expected and Meilisearch actual distributions for every public facet: make, model, trim, year, price bucket, mileage bucket, state, condition, conversion type, color, ramp type, seller type, conversion brand, and WAV features.
- [ ] Expected values apply production canonicalization before comparison.
- [ ] Reports distinguish count divergence, value-set divergence, canonicalization divergence, missing coverage, and unavailable Meilisearch.
- [ ] Coverage ratios are reported globally and by source for nullable/unknown fields.
- [ ] Required/exclusive facet invariants are explicit; optional and multi-valued facet invariants do not generate false positives.
- [ ] Historical baselines detect sudden coverage drops by source/field with configurable thresholds.
- [ ] The report includes pending/quarantined counts and `listing-resolve` backlog so publication stalls are visible.
- [ ] Output is available in concise human-readable and machine-readable forms.
- [ ] Structured logs/metrics avoid descriptions, private-seller contact data, and other unnecessary sensitive content.
- [ ] Tests cover exact match, stale index, duplicate vehicle docs, missing facet values, canonical aliases, multi-valued features, and Meilisearch unavailable.

records.title: ci: gate main image publishing on E2E and clarify CI policy
records.issueTitle: Gate main image publishing on E2E and clarify CI policy
records.issueBody:
## Context

We reviewed the current CI/merge-queue/deployment behavior and found that `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on `pull_request`, `merge_group`, and `push` to `main`.

Current behavior:
- Required merge checks are `Docker builds`, `Lint & Typecheck`, and `Test`.
- `E2E smoke` runs but is not required by branch protection.
- `Publish images (digest-pinned)` runs only on `push` to `main`.

- Recent CI usage shows E2E is still early and growing; it should not become a merge-queue blocker until the critical smoke path is better defined.

## Proposed plan for Claude/Codex review

Ask Claude and Codex to review and refine this plan before implementation:

1. Keep the current merge-queue required checks unchanged for now: `Docker builds`, `Lint & Typecheck`, and `Test`.
2. Keep `E2E smoke` running on PR, merge queue, and `main`, but do not add it to the repository ruleset yet.
3. Make `Publish images (digest-pinned)` depend on `e2e` so post-merge production image publishing only happens after E2E passes.
4. Add PR-only workflow concurrency cancellation to reduce wasted CI from superseded PR pushes, without cancelling `merge_group` or `push` runs.
5. Update deployment and merge-queue docs so the post-merge `main` CI + publish flow is explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `publish` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` depends on `e2e` in addition to `docker-done`, `lint-typecheck`, and `test`.
- [ ] `E2E smoke` remains non-required in branch protection/rulesets; no ruleset update adds it as a required merge-queue check.
- [ ] PR-only concurrency cancellation is added so newer commits to the same PR cancel older in-progress PR CI runs.
- [ ] Merge queue and `main` push runs are not cancelled by the new concurrency settings.
- [ ] `docs/ops/deployment.md` explains that `main` publishing is gated by Docker builds, lint/typecheck, tests, and E2E.
- [ ] `docs/design/merge-queue.md` explains that E2E currently runs as signal but is not yet a required merge-queue check.
- [ ] PR evidence shows `Publish images (digest-pinned)` remains skipped on PRs.
- [ ] Post-merge evidence or workflow reasoning shows `Publish images (digest-pinned)` cannot start until `E2E smoke` succeeds on `main`.

- [ ] The issue is implemented on a feature branch through the WivWav SDLC workflow.
- [ ] `pnpm check:affected` passes.
- [ ] Before finish, `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm test` passes, or any skipped check is explicitly justified in the PR.
- [ ] The PR body maps each acceptance criterion to evidence.

records.title: feat(api): single-owner search projection with zero-downtime rebuild
records.issueTitle: feat(api): single-owner search projection with zero-downtime rebuild
records.issueBody:
## Context

Ratified decision D3 in #666. Today: `apps/api/src/index.ts:99-106` runs `syncAll` on every startup, which clears the live index (`services/listing-search.ts:150-167`) and repopulates in the background — every API restart is a public-search availability window. A second, materially different rebuild exists in `apps/scraper/src/jobs/meilisearch-sync.ts` (representative-per-group). Nine scraper job files call `syncListings()` after mutations. On Meilisearch failure, `routes/listings.ts:255-268` silently drops all filters and returns HTTP 200.

## Problem / Goal

Implement the ratified invariants: PostgreSQL authoritative; exactly one projection owner; idempotent incremental updates; full rebuilds write a versioned index and atomically swap (`swapIndexes`); the live index is never cleared; API startup never rebuilds; search failure returns an explicit degraded/503 error-envelope response, never silently unfiltered results.

## Proposed approach

Phase 0 (required first): commit a written mechanism comparison — checkpointed `(updatedAt, id)` poller vs transactional outbox — using the failure-mode rubric recorded in #666 (commit/timestamp ordering, identical timestamps, non-Prisma writers, checkpoint-after-index-commit ordering, crash replay, future hard deletes). Decision rule: bounded eventual repair via reconciliation acceptable → poller; atomic no-loss capture across arbitrary writers/deletes required → outbox. Then: single indexer worker; remove startup `syncAll` and per-job `syncListings`; versioned rebuild + swap; 503 handling in the listings route; accessible degraded state in web. #642 reconciliation is the backstop in either design; align fixtures with #640/#641.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism comparison is committed and the choice recorded before implementation begins
- [ ] Exactly one code path writes the listings index in steady state; startup `syncAll` and scattered `syncListings` calls are removed
- [ ] Full rebuild writes a versioned index and swaps atomically; queries during a rebuild never observe an empty/partial index
- [ ] With Meilisearch stopped, filtered `/v1/listings` requests return an explicit degraded/503 error-envelope response
- [ ] Manual QA: the web search page shows an accessible degraded state when search is down

## Notes

From #666 (D3, ratified 2026-07-05). Expect to split into sub-issues after Phase 0; do not start implementation before the recorded mechanism decision. Supersedes the API-startup-sync behavior introduced for first-boot convenience.

## Context

The API's request/response shapes currently live in three hand-maintained places with nothing detecting drift between them:

- `packages/types` — shared interfaces consumed by web/ops
- Per-route Fastify JSON schemas — querystring only (e.g. `filterQuerySchema` in `apps/api/src/routes/listings.ts`); responses are never validated or schema-serialized
- `docs/api-routes.md` — hand-written route documentation

A route can change its response shape without any compile-time or runtime signal to consumers. Fastify has first-class support for schema-first contracts via TypeBox (`@fastify/type-provider-typebox`, MIT-licensed), which also unlocks generated OpenAPI.

## Problem / Goal

Make route schemas the single source of truth: request **and** response validation at runtime, route handler types inferred from schemas instead of duplicated, and an OpenAPI document generated from the running app. Scope this issue to the foundation plus one exemplar route group; remaining route groups convert in follow-up issues.

## Proposed approach

1. Add `@sinclair/typebox` and `@fastify/type-provider-typebox` to `apps/api`; wire the type provider in `buildApp` (`apps/api/src/app.ts`).
2. Convert `/v1/listings` (`apps/api/src/routes/listings.ts`) as the exemplar: TypeBox schemas for querystring, params, and `2xx`/error responses, preserving the `{ data: T }` / `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope exactly.
3. Register `@fastify/swagger` and expose the generated OpenAPI 3 JSON (e.g. `GET /openapi.json`).
4. Note in `docs/api-routes.md` that converted routes are documented canonically by the generated spec.
5. Follow-up (out of scope here): convert remaining route groups; consider moving schemas into `packages/types` so web/ops derive types from `Static<typeof schema>` instead of parallel interfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `buildApp` uses the TypeBox type provider; the exemplar route handlers get querystring/params/reply types inferred from schemas with no hand-written generics
- [ ] `/v1/listings` and `/v1/listings/facets` validate requests and serialize responses via TypeBox schemas, with the existing response envelope and status codes unchanged (existing route tests pass without behavioral edits)
- [ ] A generated OpenAPI 3 document is served from the API and includes the converted routes
- [ ] Runtime dependency licenses remain MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD

## Notes

Response schemas also switch serialization to `fast-json-stringify` on converted routes, which is a modest performance win. Related: `docs/api-routes.md` stays authoritative for unconverted routes until the follow-up migration completes.

records.title: fix(web): stop flaky/false-positive a11y focus-order e2e tests
records.issueTitle: bug(web): E2E accessibility smoke fails — StateHeatMap geography paths lack visible focus indicator
records.issueBody:
## Context
CI's \`E2E smoke\` job (\`e2e/tests/accessibility.spec.ts\`) has been failing on \`main\` since the accessibility-gates commit (9e28228, \"chore(infra): add accessibility gates (fixes #673)\"), and continues to fail at the latest \`main\` HEAD (d78aea0). Confirmed independent of unrelated PR work: the same failure reproduces on \`main\` outside of any feature branch, so it is not a flake introduced by another change.

## Problem / Goal
Two accessibility smoke tests fail because keyboard-only Tab navigation through the state heat map (\`StateHeatMap-module\`) lands on \`rsm-geography\` \`<path>\` elements (state shapes, \`tabindex="0"\`) that have no visible focus indicator (no outline/box-shadow, and no stroke-width change on focus).

Failing tests:
- \`[chromium] › tests/accessibility.spec.ts:133:3 › accessibility smoke (axe) › keyboard-only pass: discover has an in-order, visible focus sequence\`
- \`[chromium] › tests/accessibility.spec.ts:140:3 › accessibility smoke (axe) › keyboard-only pass: results has an in-order, visible focus sequence\`

Assertion failure (from \`assertTabOrderHasVisibleFocus\`, e2e/tests/accessibility.spec.ts:124):
\`\`\`
Error: stop 4 (<path tabindex="0" class="rsm-geography StateHeatMap-module__wjCmNW__state" d="...">) has no visible focus indicator
expect(hasVisibleFocus).toBe(true)
Received: false
\`\`\`

The state heat map component is likely in \`apps/web\` (module name \`StateHeatMap-module\`); needs a \`:focus-visible\` style (outline, box-shadow, or stroke-width bump) applied to the \`rsm-geography\` path elements.

## Proposed approach
- Locate the \`StateHeatMap\` component (CSS module \`StateHeatMap-module\`) in \`apps/web\`.
- Add a visible \`:focus-visible\` style to \`.rsm-geography\` / the state path elements — e.g. an outline, box-shadow, or increased stroke-width relative to the baseline (matching whatever mechanism \`assertTabOrderHasVisibleFocus\` checks: \`outline\`, \`boxShadow\`, or \`focusedStrokeWidth > baselineStrokeWidth\`).
- Re-run \`pnpm test:e2e\` (or the \`accessibility.spec.ts\` file directly) locally against a built container to confirm both failing tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \`[chromium] › tests/accessibility.spec.ts:133:3\` (discover heat map focus sequence) passes locally and in CI
- [ ] \`[chromium] › tests/accessibility.spec.ts:140:3\` (results heat map focus sequence) passes locally and in CI
- [ ] Manual QA: tabbing through the state heat map on \`/discover\` and \`/results\` in a browser shows a clearly visible focus ring/outline on each state as it receives keyboard focus

## Notes
Confirmed on \`main\` at commit d78aea0 (CI run 28900167133) and at 9e28228 (CI run 28891756569) — not a transient flake, not introduced by unrelated branch work. First observed while validating PR #691 (issue #667), which is unrelated in scope; do not conflate the two.

records.title: chore(infra): automated PostgreSQL backups, tested restore drill, and Valkey state audit
records.issueTitle: chore(infra): automated PostgreSQL backups, tested restore drill, and Valkey state audit
records.issueBody:
## Context

Ratified decision D8 in #666. PostgreSQL is the authoritative store, and its contents are not fully re-scrapable: `ListingPriceHistory`/`ListingMileageHistory`/`ListingConversionHistory`, human vehicle-identity decisions, and encrypted app config exist only in this database. No backup, restore procedure, or RPO/RTO exists anywhere in the repository. Valkey cannot yet be declared ephemeral: operator mutations via `/admin/repeatables` change BullMQ state held only in Valkey, and no schedule model exists in `schema.prisma`.

## Problem / Goal

1. Automated durable PostgreSQL backups with documented RPO/RTO, retention, and encryption/access policy.
2. A restore drill that restores a backup into a clean environment and verifies application-level invariants.
3. A Valkey state audit that classifies every Valkey-resident state class (pending jobs, repeatable schedules, operator overrides) and records the ratified decision: move intent into an authoritative store (aligns with the D5 declarative registry) or define a persistence/backup policy.

## Proposed approach

Decide backup tooling (pg_dump schedule vs WAL-based) and destination once the D6 deployment definition exists; add a compose service or scheduled job; write the runbook under `docs/data/`; script the restore drill; produce the Valkey audit as a short document plus follow-up issue if intent moves to PostgreSQL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A scheduled job produces durable PostgreSQL backups automatically, with RPO/RTO, retention, and access policy documented
- [ ] A documented, scripted restore drill restores a backup into a clean environment and verifies invariants: listing/history row counts, vehicle-identity decisions present, encrypted config decryptable with the correct secret
- [ ] The Valkey state audit is committed, every state class classified, and schedule-intent ownership recorded as a decision

## Notes

From #666 (D8, ratified 2026-07-05). Beta-blocking, peer to #599/#600/#658. Backup destination depends on the D6 deployment definition issue.

records.title: chore(infra): add Dependabot version and security updates
records.issueTitle: chore(infra): add Dependabot version and security updates
records.issueBody:
## Context

Nothing watches the repo's dependencies for updates or published CVEs. The monorepo spans ~14 workspaces (pnpm), five Dockerfiles, and several GitHub Actions workflows — a vulnerable transitive dependency would sit unnoticed until someone manually runs an audit. The repo is public, so both Dependabot and the CI runs its PRs trigger are free. Renovate was considered and deferred; Dependabot chosen for zero-infrastructure setup (decision 2026-07-03).

## Problem / Goal

Add a `.github/dependabot.yml` covering all three ecosystems in the repo, grouped so routine updates arrive as one weekly PR instead of a dozen, and enable Dependabot security updates so CVE fixes open PRs immediately regardless of schedule.

## Proposed approach

1. Create `.github/dependabot.yml` with three entries:
   - `package-ecosystem: npm`, `directory: /` — pnpm workspace root (Dependabot resolves `pnpm-lock.yaml` from the root for all workspaces)
   - `package-ecosystem: docker`, `directory: /docker` — base images in the five Dockerfiles
   - `package-ecosystem: github-actions`, `directory: /` — action versions in `.github/workflows/`
2. Group npm minor + patch bumps into a single weekly PR via `groups:`; leave majors as individual PRs. Weekly schedule for docker and github-actions too.
3. Enable **Dependabot alerts** and **Dependabot security updates** in repo settings (not configurable from the yml).
4. Confirm the first scheduled run's PRs trigger the full CI (docker builds, lint, typecheck, tests) like any other PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/dependabot.yml` exists covering npm (workspace root), docker (`/docker`), and github-actions ecosystems
- [ ] npm minor/patch updates are grouped into one weekly PR; major updates open individually
- [ ] Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled in repository settings
- [ ] A Dependabot-opened PR runs the full CI pipeline and is mergeable via the normal merge queue (`gh pr merge --auto`)

## Notes

License policy constraint: reviewers must still check license changes on major bumps (runtime deps limited to MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/PostgreSQL; never GPL/AGPL) — Dependabot does not enforce this. Renovate remains the fallback if grouping proves too coarse for the monorepo; rejected for now to avoid a third-party app. Related: architecture review of 2026-07-02 (#598, #599, #600).

records.title: test(infra): add built-container e2e smoke suite
records.issueTitle: test(infra): add Playwright E2E smoke suite against the built containers
records.issueBody:
## Context

There are no end-to-end tests: Playwright exists in the repo only as the scraper's fetching tool, and no `playwright.config.*` exists for web or ops. The cost of this gap is already on `main`: #595 (fixed in fc28c67) shipped a web container missing `public/` — a failure class that only exists in the built image and is invisible to every unit test. CI builds all four images on every PR (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` docker matrix) but never boots them.

## Problem / Goal

Add a small Playwright smoke suite that boots the built containers via docker compose and drives the critical public flows, so container-assembly and cross-service integration breaks block merge instead of reaching deploy.

## Proposed approach

1. New top-level `e2e/` workspace with `@playwright/test` (Apache-2.0) and a `test:e2e` script.
2. Boot the stack from the built images with docker compose (postgres, meilisearch, valkey, api, web; seed minimal fixture data or assert empty states).
3. Smoke specs — keep it to ~5:
   - home page renders with static assets served (direct regression test for #595)
   - Discover/search flow returns results or a well-formed empty state
   - listing detail page loads
   - `/health` reports healthy across dependencies
4. CI job that reuses the existing buildx GHA cache scopes, boots compose, runs the suite, and uploads Playwright traces on failure.
5. Document local usage (`pnpm test:e2e`) in `AGENTS.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Playwright smoke suite runs against the **built** web and api containers via docker compose, not `next dev`
- [ ] Suite covers home render (including a static asset from `public/`), the Discover search flow, and a listing detail page
- [ ] CI runs the suite on PRs, blocks merge on failure, and uploads traces/screenshots as artifacts on failure
- [ ] Local run is a single documented command

## Notes

Ordering: independent of #598/#599 and can land first — it reuses images CI already builds. Keep the suite intentionally tiny; breadth belongs to unit tests (#419) and the integration tier (#599).

records.title: test(api): add integration test tier for repositories, search sync, and cache
records.issueTitle: test(api): add integration test tier running repositories against real Postgres, Meilisearch, and Valkey
records.issueBody:
## Context

Every database-touching test in the repo mocks its infrastructure: repository tests stub `PrismaClient` with `vi.fn()` (e.g. `apps/api/src/repositories/listing-repository.test.ts` asserts the shape of the `findMany` call, not that the query returns correct rows), and no test file anywhere constructs a real `PrismaClient`. Raw-SQL paths (`$queryRaw` in the listing/market repositories) are entirely unverified against a real database. Meilisearch and Valkey behavior is likewise only ever mocked.

CI already provisions a real Postgres 17 service container, applies migrations, and checks schema drift (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` test job) — but nothing ever executes a query against it. Meilisearch and Valkey are absent from CI entirely.

## Problem / Goal

Add a separate integration test tier that exercises the Prisma repositories, Meilisearch sync, and Valkey cache against real services, so query bugs, index-mapping bugs, and cache-behavior bugs are caught in CI instead of production.

## Proposed approach

1. Add a `test:integration` turbo task, kept separate from `test` so the unit suite stays runnable with no infrastructure.
2. `apps/api`: integration specs for the Prisma repositories against the migrated database from `DATABASE_URL`, prioritizing the `$queryRaw` paths in `listing-repository.ts` and `market-repository.ts`; reset state between tests (truncate or per-test transaction).
3. `packages/search`: `syncListings()` and query round-trip against a real Meilisearch (covers the untested error/mapping paths flagged in #265).
4. `apps/api` cache service (`services/cache/`): get/set/invalidate round-trip against real Valkey.
5. CI: add `meilisearch` and `valkey` service containers beside the existing `postgres` service; run `pnpm test:integration` after the existing migrate + drift steps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pnpm test:integration` runs repository tests against a real, migrated Postgres with no Prisma mocks
- [ ] Every `$queryRaw` repository method has at least one integration test asserting real result rows
- [ ] Meilisearch listing sync and Valkey cache round-trips are covered against real service containers
- [ ] CI runs the integration tier with service containers and failures block merge
- [ ] `pnpm test` (unit tier) still passes with no databases running

## Notes

Complements #265 (unit-level coverage for `packages/search`/`queue`/`db`) — this issue is about the execution environment, not coverage breadth. The CI drift check already guarantees migrations match `schema.prisma`, so the integration tier can assume a migrated database.
